a103.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a103.name: Donald Trump
a103.title: President of the United States
a103.speech: Announced a temporary 90-day suspension of certain international funding, a measure described as a "period of strategic evaluation" of international priorities.

a143.speaker: Brookings Institution report (containing UN data)
a143.name: Brookings Institution report (containing UN data)
a143.speech: Shows that Malawi is on track on just one of the 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals, representing a paltry 2.7 percent success rate, and that globally, 17 percent of the targets are on track while about 35 percent are stagnating or regressing; further shows that progress on goals number one and 15 has stagnated while on goals two, four, five, seven, eight, 11, 12, 16 and 17, the country has been on the decline.

a143.speaker: Ahunna Eziakonwa, UN assistant secretary general and UN Development Programme regional bureau for Africa director
a143.name: Ahunna Eziakonwa
a143.title: UN assistant secretary general and UN Development Programme regional bureau for Africa director
a143.speech: Is quoted in the report as having said that out of 17 SDGs, Malawi is only on track on goal number 10 on reducing inequalities.

a143.speaker: Ahunna Eziakonwa, UN assistant secretary general and UN Development Programme regional bureau for Africa director
a143.name: Ahunna Eziakonwa
a143.title: UN assistant secretary general and UN Development Programme regional bureau for Africa director
a143.speech: Said reversing this troubling trajectory in Africa will require a new bold strategic approach, adequate and affordable financing and renewed political commitment: “African countries must also prioritise efficiency enhancements in domestic development spending, which far exceeds aid dollars. Additionally, the financing of strategic investments [particularly infrastructure, energy, and technology] requires increased ingenuity and ambition. Improving public financial management and closing tax/contractual loopholes could generate almost twice the amount of Official Development Assistance [ODA] that African countries currently receive.”

a143.speaker: Hanan Morsy, UN Economic Commission for Africa (Uneca) deputy executive secretary and chief economist
a143.name: Hanan Morsy
a143.title: UN Economic Commission for Africa (Uneca) deputy executive secretary and chief economist
a143.speech: Said among the several factors required to accelerate progress toward the SDGs, availability of development finance or investment in the SDGs is the most critical: “First, domestic resource mobilisation remains limited, with many African economies struggling with narrow tax bases, tax evasion and inefficiencies in public financial management. Secondly, the high debt burden of many African nations has crowded out public investment in critical sectors such as health care, education and infrastructure, undermining efforts to achieve the SDGs.”

a143.speaker: UN Economic Commission for Africa (Uneca) estimates
a143.name: UN Economic Commission for Africa (Uneca) estimates
a143.speech: According to estimates by Uneca, successful implementation of the SDGs would require $1.3 trillion annually, of which it is estimated African countries could mobilise a little over 50 percent, leaving a huge financing gap.

a143.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a143.name: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a143.speech: Said this gap has been worsened by global economic downturns, the Covid-19 pandemic and climate change-related catastrophes, creating significant pressure on national budgets and development efforts across the continent, making it difficult for countries to achieve SDGs.

a143.speaker: Velli Nyirongo, Scotland-based Malawian economist
a143.name: Velli Nyirongo
a143.title: Scotland-based Malawian economist
a143.speech: Said in an interview that given the country’s current economic structure and challenges, it would be difficult for the country to fully bridge the financing gap through domestic means to achieve SDGs: “A multi-faceted approach combining domestic resource mobilisation, improved tax administration, foreign aid, concessional loans and private sector engagement is necessary to address the financing needs effectively.”

a143.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a143.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a143.title: President of Malawi
a143.speech: Speaking at a meeting with global partners and investors during the Malawi Partners Conference on the sidelines of the 78th United Nations General Assembly Conference in New York last year, appealed for more support from development partners, financial institutions and other advanced countries to assist Malawi to achieve the SDGs by 2030.

a143.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a143.name: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a143.speech: Said last year that given the current inflows of financing, Malawi faced a gap of about $3.59 billion (about K6.2 trillion) or $0.63 billion (K1.1 trillion) annually to fast-track structural transformation for the 2030 Agenda for SDGs; AfDB data show that in 2022, ODA flows for Malawi amounted to $926.1 million in 2021 while net portfolio investments were negative since 2019.

a183.speaker: Senior Guinean administration official (anonymous)
a183.name: Senior Guinean administration official (anonymous)
a183.speech: Comments: "The decision has no impact on the ongoing demographic and health survey (the official launch of the demographic and health survey took place on Wednesday 7 November 2024 in Conakry). The survey is continuing in accordance with the established timetable. In fact, the part covered by USAID is already completed. What remains to be done is financed by another partner..."

a183.speaker: Trump administration (official justification)
a183.name: Trump administration (official justification)
a183.speech: The official reasons given for targeting USAID: mismanagement, forcing "woke" philosophy such as transgenderism and homosexuality, support for countries hostile to the United States.

a183.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a183.name: Marco Rubio
a183.title: US Secretary of State
a183.speech: Was the first to order the suspension for 3 months of all foreign aid as soon as he took office on 24 January 2025.

a183.speaker: Elon Musk, head of DOGE (posts on X)
a183.name: Elon Musk
a183.title: head of DOGE (posts on X)
a183.speech: He leaked information accusing USAID of "fanciful" funding and describing the agency as a "criminal organisation" on his social network X.

a183.speaker: US Embassy in Conakry and Guinean Ministry of Cooperation (non-response)
a183.name: US Embassy in Conakry and Guinean Ministry of Cooperation (non-response)
a183.speech: Guineenews sought to contact the United States embassy in Conakry as well as the ministry of cooperation, but was unable to obtain a response as we go to press.

a210.name: Tahliil Axmed Fiidow Caraale (also known as Cali Daahir Jimcaale)
a210.title: defendant, former member of the armed forces
a210.speech: Said that 'AS' (Al-Shabaab) cut off his hand after he indicated that he had been accused of theft.

a210.name: Office of the Prosecutor of the Military Court (Armed Forces Court)
a210.speech: Requested that a severe sentence be imposed on Tahliil Axmed Fiidow, since the explosion he was accused of caused deaths.

a210.speaker: The defendant and his lawyers
a210.name: The defendant and his lawyers
a210.speech: Jointly requested for their part that the punishment be reduced in the cases the prosecution had charged him with, given that he had confessed to part of the crimes he is accused of.

a210.speaker: Chairman Shuute, presiding judge of the Armed Forces Court
a210.name: Chairman Shuute
a210.title: presiding judge of the Armed Forces Court

a267.speaker: International Rescue Committee (IRC) report
a267.name: International Rescue Committee (IRC) report
a267.speech: Almost five million people could be plunged into hunger and famine as a fourth round of desert locusts hatch and ravage crops across the Horn and East Africa, compounding an already dire food situation worsened by the COVID-19 pandemic; another round of hatching could produce swarms up to 8,000 times larger than the first generation earlier this year. The IRC is calling for a major ramp up of preventive measures to stop the swarms from destroying lives and spreading across West Africa and to the Indo-Pakistan border.

a267.speaker: Barri Shorey, Senior Director of Economic Recovery for the IRC
a267.name: Barri Shorey
a267.title: Senior Director of Economic Recovery for the IRC
a267.speech: "the Desert Locust is the world's most dangerous migratory pest. A one-square-kilometer locust swarm is capable of consuming the same amount of food in one day as approximately 35,000 people. The worst outbreak in 70 years is combined with a year of drought and flooding, and now a COVID-19 pandemic preventing people from working and farming, poses an unprecedented risk to food security. Without an immediate increase of prevention measures, we could be on the verge of a famine like we have never seen before."

a267.speaker: Sahal Farah, Community Resilience Committee Vice Chairman for Docol, an IRC partner organization
a267.name: Sahal Farah
a267.title: Community Resilience Committee Vice Chairman for Docol, an IRC partner organization
a267.speech: "this is the worst locust invasion we have seen in our generation; it has destroyed pastures, contaminated water sources and displaced many pastoral households. The worst part is that we do not have the capacity to control it, and so far, we have not received any external support."

a267.speaker: Food and Agriculture Organization
a267.name: Food and Agriculture Organization
a267.speech: predicts a 50-70 percent cereal harvest loss in Somalia without intervention.

a267.speaker: International Rescue Committee (IRC)
a267.name: International Rescue Committee (IRC)
a267.speech: estimates that 5,000 households, especially those headed by women, currently do or will need urgent humanitarian assistance by August if harvests fail and market prices rise; says it is scaling up multipurpose cash assistance and farming support to reach all 5,000 at risk households and has launched a US 30 million appeal to help mitigate the spread of coronavirus among the world's most vulnerable populations.

a385.speaker: Colonel Massalatchi Mahaman Sani, Governor of the Zinder Region
a385.name: Colonel Massalatchi Mahaman Sani
a385.title: Governor of the Zinder Region
a385.speech: Praised the diligence of the education authorities, the supervisors and the students, urging them to maintain rigour and discipline during the examinations ; also stressed the importance of these qualifications in easing young people's entry into the labour market, in a national context seeking qualified workers.

a385.speaker: Colonel Massalatchi Mahaman Sani, Governor of the Zinder Region
a385.name: Colonel Massalatchi Mahaman Sani
a385.title: Governor of the Zinder Region
a385.speech: "For those who are going to do sport, try to give your maximum, this is not a war. Do not exceed your capacities and give the best of yourselves. For those who are physically unable, you will take your written test in a room. Act as if you were on the field, take your time, read carefully and show the best of yourselves."

a805.speaker: Mohamed Mehdi Bensaid, Moroccan Minister of Culture, Youth and Communication
a805.name: Mohamed Mehdi Bensaid
a805.title: Moroccan Minister of Culture, Youth and Communication
a805.speech: Praised the pivotal role played by the Maghreb Arab Press agency (MAP) in the media field, highlighting the positive developments the agency has continued to bring to the media sector in Morocco; affirmed the ministry's determination to support MAP in carrying out its projects to meet the new challenges it faces.

a805.speaker: Rachid Boumahil, Secretary-General of the Maghreb Arab Press agency (MAP)
a805.name: Rachid Boumahil
a805.title: Secretary-General of the Maghreb Arab Press agency (MAP)
a805.speech: Reviewed, in a presentation given on the occasion, the achievements made by the agency during 2020, a year marked by an unprecedented situation: a general lockdown, travel restrictions throughout the year, and a halt of activity in many economic sectors ; recalled, while highlighting MAP's international leadership, that the agency will organise the seventh session of the General Assembly of the World Congress of News Agencies in 2022 in Marrakech.

a807.speaker: United Kingdom (UK)
a807.name: United Kingdom (UK)
a807.speech: Has reaffirmed its commitment to a modern and equal partnership with Malawi after the two nations clocked 60 years of formal ties.

a807.speaker: Fiona Ritchie, British High Commissioner to Malawi
a807.name: Fiona Ritchie
a807.title: British High Commissioner to Malawi
a807.speech: Stressed on the importance of building on the existing relations to address emerging challenges affecting the two countries; highlighted the need to address contemporary challenges in areas such as technology, trade and climate action. Said Ritchie: “At its core, our partnership is not about dependency or charity. A modern partnership goes beyond aid. I hope to see more collaboration in various areas to deliver our shared objectives. With the right choices, Malawi’s future is bright and I am optimistic about the next 60 years of this partnership.” ; added that for future collaborations, the UK will prioritise modern solutions to persistent challenges, acknowledging that it is clearly what Malawians want.

a807.speaker: Fiona Ritchie, British High Commissioner to Malawi
a807.name: Fiona Ritchie
a807.title: British High Commissioner to Malawi
a807.speech: Called for peaceful and transparent elections, adding the UK is ready to provide support to Malawi’s democratic institutions and society to ensure every citizen exercises the right to vote: “Next years’ elections are an important opportunity for Malawi to further consolidate its democratic record, I hope that Malawians will remain peaceful and tolerant throughout the process.”

a807.speaker: Nancy Tembo, Malawi Minister of Foreign Affairs
a807.name: Nancy Tembo
a807.title: Malawi Minister of Foreign Affairs
a807.speech: Acknowledged the UK as one of Malawi’s most reliable development partners, highlighting contributions to key sectors including health, education and governance; noted the UK’s increased support, particularly in public finance management which has helped Malawi secure the International Monetary Fund’s Extended Credit Facility, tripling its Official Development Assistance to Malawi from 16.3 million euro (about K30 billion) in the 2023/24 financial year to 51 million euro (about K93.9 billion) for the 2024/2025 financial year: “This significant increase reflects the importance of the UK’s partnership with Malawi and the UK’s commitment to supporting the Malawi 2063.”

a1005.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, Somali President
a1005.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a1005.title: Somali President
a1005.speech: Recently announced the construction of the new Mogadishu city, a process that will bring potential new opportunities for the private sector and contribute to deepening Turkiye-Somalia relations.

a1368.speaker: Peter Madeleka, lawyer with the Stalwart firm, representing the 36 women
a1368.name: Peter Madeleka
a1368.title: lawyer with the Stalwart firm, representing the 36 women
a1368.speech: Confirmed that they had already delivered the notice to the district commissioner: "It is true I have written him a 14-day notice, because in a civil claim the first step is to write a notice of intention to sue the person you are claiming from. Those 14 days begin today after receipt, and he is required to pay my clients Sh36 billion for humiliating them." ; said that once the notice is received he is legally required to respond, and if he does not agree to pay his clients that amount within that period they intend to go to court to file a case ; "My clients were arrested by the district commissioner contrary to the law and stayed in police custody at Mburahati for more than five days accused of prostitution, but they were not taken to court for it to be proven whether they engage in prostitution; rather, it is oppression that was done." ; said the Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) failed to bring them to court, ended up taking them to his office, and later they were taken by the Police before being released ; responding to Bomboko's denial, he said: "That is his opinion."

a1368.speaker: Hassan Bomboko, Ubungo District Commissioner
a1368.name: Hassan Bomboko
a1368.title: Ubungo District Commissioner
a1368.speech: Speaking to Mwananchi, said that as of 11:48 a.m. that day he had not received the notice said to have been sent to him: "I have not received that notice. Ask them properly." When contacted again in the evening he could not be reached.

a1368.speaker: 14-day legal notice served on the Ubungo District Commissioner (document seen by Mwananchi Digital)
a1368.name: 14-day legal notice served on the Ubungo District Commissioner (document seen by Mwananchi Digital)
a1368.speech: The notice, starting Thursday, June 20, 2024, seeks payment of Sh36 billion to the 36 suspects, who claim they were humiliated by being called 'Dada Poa' and held in custody for more than five days contrary to the law.

a1368.speaker: Some women's rights activists
a1368.name: Some women's rights activists
a1368.speech: Have criticised the operation, saying it violates human rights.

a1368.speaker: Albert Chalamila, Dar es Salaam Regional Commissioner
a1368.name: Albert Chalamila
a1368.title: Dar es Salaam Regional Commissioner
a1368.speech: Speaking at the commemoration of the Day of the African Child, defended Bomboko over the ongoing social media debates criticising the arrest operation; said he had gone through social media and seen blame being directed at the Ubungo district commissioner's action of arresting 'dada poa' and 'kaka poa' ; "Now, through this Day of the African Child, I ask, in few words and with great severity, to clarify the following. In the discussions about children, they have shown that it is important to receive parental upbringing, but it is a disgrace for Tanzania and other African countries to interpret ordinary life as a mother or father selling themselves for much of their lives and forgetting the upbringing of children." ; said what is being done now is to begin changing people's attitudes, while within the councils preparations have begun for a special loan scheme to help those thinking of selling their bodies to start businesses instead; warned against cheering on what he called foolishness, and asked non-governmental institutions to recognise that these children have no other father, but their father is Africa, which will raise them to be good leaders.

a1368.speaker: Albert Chalamila, Dar es Salaam Regional Commissioner
a1368.name: Albert Chalamila
a1368.title: Dar es Salaam Regional Commissioner
a1368.speech: Said those who feel the women were humiliated are wrong, because no one was stripped of their clothes; rather, they undressed themselves: "Not a single woman had such things done to her; rather, they were taken as they had dressed themselves, sitting in public before the people themselves, and taken to a place so that it would not be a shame for children going to school at dawn." ; "Some Form One and Form Two children who were arrested in the areas while selling themselves said they had copied the behaviour of their mothers and fathers."

a1368.speaker: Albert Chalamila, Dar es Salaam Regional Commissioner
a1368.name: Albert Chalamila
a1368.title: Dar es Salaam Regional Commissioner
a1368.speech: Said that on the eve of the Eid holiday a four-year-old child was sodomised at home while alone after the parents had gone out, while another, aged nine, was raped; said state organs are following up on those who committed those acts while the children's health is being monitored despite them already being psychologically affected ; "These stories, if you listen to them carefully, awaken in us the zeal of fathers and mothers to be great lovers of upbringing for our children, and we should never be fans of acts that degrade the dignity of a woman, the dignity of a child, or the dignity of a citizen." ; said a child is the capital for the growth of the future nation, and that just as a person invests in business for the pride of old age, it is time to invest in children as the pride of the future nation.

a1368.speaker: Dr Hellen Kijo Bisimba, human rights activist
a1368.name: Dr Hellen Kijo Bisimba
a1368.title: human rights activist
a1368.speech: Said what is being done is interference with people's privacy contrary to the Constitution of the United Republic: "Even if the aim is to protect morals, interfering with people's privacy is an offence under the law." ; explaining further, said the laws are ambiguous in controlling the prostitution business: "The Penal Code says that the person who uses proceeds derived from prostitution is the one committing an offence. Why should those who buy 'dada poa' not be at fault? If a woman sells her body, it means there is a buyer. How do you know that this one is selling herself? Because others are just passers-by."

a1532.speaker: Namibian Police (at the drug destruction event)
a1532.name: Namibian Police (at the drug destruction event)
a1532.speech: Highlighted several hurdles that prolong drug-related investigation processes.

a1532.speaker: Becker, Namibian Police forensic official
a1532.name: Becker
a1532.title: Namibian Police forensic official
a1532.speech: Said the destroyed consignment originated from a major bust at the Walvis Bay port in 2018.

a1532.speaker: Becker, Namibian Police forensic official
a1532.name: Becker
a1532.title: Namibian Police forensic official
a1532.speech: "Since last year October, and even a year before this, we cannot do any analysis on cocaine because the National Police of Namibia are having problems importing drug standards into the country. This is a minute amount of pure drugs, in layman's terms, used for analysis to establish what drug we are dealing with" ; "We have been struggling to get a permit or licence from the Namibia Medicines Regulatory Council (NMRC) to be able to bring the standard into the country and store it in our facility" ; said the absence of a drug standard in Namibia prolongs several drug-related cases for years, even though it only takes one day to carry out the test ; "There is one supplier of these standards in South Africa and we could not get them to deliver a performance guarantee to us so that we could make an advance payment, which they insisted on" ; "We are a credible institution, part of the Namibian government. Currently, the health ministry is trying to generate an order for us, but we are at the end of the financial year, with little hope that this will happen soon."

a1532.speaker: Becker, Namibian Police forensic official
a1532.name: Becker
a1532.title: Namibian Police forensic official
a1532.speech: Said that at the moment they only dispose of drugs once a year but would ideally like to start doing so after every drug-related case has been closed ; revealed that the Forensics Institute made a payment of N$137 000 to the health ministry to procure the standard, which consists of several drug testing specimens.

a1532.speaker: High Court of Namibia / Judge Orben Sibeya (court record)
a1532.name: High Court of Namibia / Judge Orben Sibeya (court record)
a1532.speech: In October 2022 sentenced Grant Noble and Dinath Azhar, caught smuggling 412 kilograms of cocaine at Walvis Bay, to 12 years in prison each.

a1532.speaker: Ben Nangombe, Executive Director of Namibia's health ministry
a1532.name: Ben Nangombe
a1532.title: Executive Director of Namibia's health ministry
a1532.speech: Told Namibian Sun that the ministry is in the process of procuring the drug standard and bringing it to Namibia: "We had an engagement and informed the Medicines Council to make provision for the funds so that the Forensics Institute could get the standard" ; said other challenges were encountered with the supplier in South Africa: "The forensics team then asked the ministry to step in again and assist with the procurement, and so we saw that the law in Namibia indeed makes provision for us to procure that specific standard. The process is still ongoing. Authorisation for the procurement has been granted, but we don't have a timeline for when it will be done."

a1551.speaker: The Rwandan government
a1551.name: The Rwandan government
a1551.speech: Has denied allegations that it provided military assistance and logistical support to the M23 rebel group.

a1551.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General
a1551.name: Antonio Guterres
a1551.title: UN Secretary-General
a1551.speech: "Peacekeeping is a remarkable exercise in international solidarity. It is a testament to our collective commitment to peace and security."

a1566.speaker: Mthuli Ncube, Zimbabwe Finance Minister
a1566.name: Mthuli Ncube
a1566.title: Zimbabwe Finance Minister
a1566.speech: Said the government is pursuing a “cost recovery” plan for Zesa Holdings (Zesa) in 2022, meaning power tariffs are set to go up.

a1582.speaker: Antony Blinken, US Secretary of State
a1582.name: Antony Blinken
a1582.title: US Secretary of State
a1582.speech: Has said that overcoming poisonous grievances and ethnic divisions is the only way to break the cycle of political and ethnic violence in Ethiopia ; "We have been talking a lot, of course, about the very important cessation of hostilities in Tigray, which has produced very significant benefits, but one aspect of that is, of course, the importance of transitional justice and accountability, making sure that the rights of every Ethiopian are protected."

a1582.speaker: Antony Blinken, US Secretary of State
a1582.name: Antony Blinken
a1582.title: US Secretary of State
a1582.speech: Announced a new humanitarian assistance package for Ethiopia for 2023: "We're going to be providing an addition $331 million (R6 billion) in assistance through this joint emergency operations programme to try to reach more people in Ethiopia who are in need of food security, and we think we'll reach another 13 million or so people being affected by drought in particular."

a1582.speaker: Antony Blinken, US Secretary of State
a1582.name: Antony Blinken
a1582.title: US Secretary of State
a1582.speech: Noted that aid to Tigray had increased and basic services were gradually being restored: "Humanitarian assistance is flowing, finally reaching nearly all communities in need; services are being restored in the Tigray region; the TPLF is disarming; Eritrean and other non-federal forces are departing. The dedicated diplomacy of the mediators from the African Union (AU), from Kenya, from South Africa, supported by the United States, was essential to securing this agreement. And the AU monitoring mechanism is a key to its full implementation."

a1582.speaker: US State Department (statement)
a1582.name: US State Department (statement)
a1582.speech: Said Blinken and Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed "discussed the significant progress in implementing the Cessation of Hostilities Agreement following the silencing of the guns in northern Ethiopia" ; said of the meeting with the peace deal signatories, "They spoke about the importance of the Disarmament, Demobilisation and Reintegration programme and the need for it to be fully developed and implemented."

a1582.speaker: Redwan Hussein, Ethiopia's National Security Advisor, and Getachew Reda, Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) spokesperson
a1582.name: Redwan Hussein
a1582.title: Ethiopia's National Security Advisor, and Getachew Reda, Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) spokesperson
a1582.speech: Shared the progress being made with the peace deal, outlining the improvements made in the silencing of guns, delivery of humanitarian assistance, restoration of services as well as the removal of Tigrayan heavy weapons and the withdrawal of Eritrean forces. They said a lot of work was still needed regarding the Pretoria Cessation of Hostilities Agreement (COHA).

a1582.speaker: Signatories of the Ethiopia peace deal
a1582.name: Signatories of the Ethiopia peace deal
a1582.speech: Have reiterated their commitment to peace and accepted the need for accountability and transitional justice.

a1969.speaker: United States government
a1969.name: United States government
a1969.speech: Decided to temporarily stop sending financial aid while it reviews its foreign assistance programmes; the US says it wants to make sure its aid is being used effectively.

a1983.speaker: Israel Defense Forces / Israeli army (statement)
a1983.name: Israel Defense Forces / Israeli army (statement)
a1983.speech: Announced in a statement that it had begun a series of attacks against Hamas terrorist targets in the southern Gaza Strip, alleging it was responding to a "flagrant violation" of the ceasefire by Hamas; Israel justifies the attacks as a response to Hamas gunfire.

a1983.speaker: Hamas
a1983.name: Hamas
a1983.speech: Denies the accusations and insists that it remains committed to the ceasefire.

a2077.speaker: Frantz Fanon (quoted)
a2077.name: Frantz Fanon (quoted)
a2077.speech: "the future will have no pity for those men, who, possessing the exceptional privilege of being able to speak words of truth to their oppressors but have, instead, taken refuge in an attitude of passivity, of mute indifference, and sometimes, of cold complicity"

a2098.speaker: Virginia E. Palmer, US Ambassador to Ghana (2022-2025) (op-ed)
a2098.name: Virginia E. Palmer
a2098.title: US Ambassador to Ghana (2022-2025) (op-ed)
a2098.speech: Writes "a love letter to Ghana: in praise of her democracy, stability, warmth and entrepreneurialism but most of all tolerance - between faiths, between ethnic groups, even between political rivals" ; says she witnessed this tolerance first-hand when she saw Ghanaian civil society organisations, academics and national leaders defend the principle of human rights for all, and when she had the honour of getting to know the National Chief Imam ; says "Ghana continues to lead the way for West Africa and beyond - from forging a path to independence nearly 70 years ago to serving as a regional model for stability and inclusive growth."

a2098.speaker: Virginia E. Palmer, US Ambassador to Ghana (2022-2025) (op-ed)
a2098.name: Virginia E. Palmer
a2098.title: US Ambassador to Ghana (2022-2025) (op-ed)
a2098.speech: Says "the future of the US/Ghana relationship is bright, underpinned by our shared commitment to the free market and democratic values"; warns that "Where some West African countries contend with democracies more nominal than real, beset with corruption or unconstitutional changes of government, their peoples are deprived of the prosperity and promise that flourishes in transparent and accountable democracies the world over" and that "Our strategic adversaries are working hard to erode public trust in democracy and accountable government institutions, making unsubstantiated claims and even encouraging restrictions on free speech" ; says historic elections in 2024 in both countries "again gave voice to the electorate - and proved that democracy is still winning."

a2098.speaker: Virginia E. Palmer, US Ambassador to Ghana (2022-2025) (op-ed)
a2098.name: Virginia E. Palmer
a2098.title: US Ambassador to Ghana (2022-2025) (op-ed)
a2098.speech: Says "Ghana and the US share a belief in the power of trade to lift their economies and their people" and that "The US remains Ghana's steadfast partner for trade"; salutes "President Mahama's commitment - declared in his inaugural address and many times since - to fight corruption and improve the business and investment climate"; notes that more than 100 U.S. companies operate in Ghana and that these American companies, along with the US Embassy and the American Chamber of Commerce, "stand ready to support Ghana's private sector-led economic restoration."

a2098.speaker: Virginia E. Palmer, US Ambassador to Ghana (2022-2025) (op-ed)
a2098.name: Virginia E. Palmer
a2098.title: US Ambassador to Ghana (2022-2025) (op-ed)
a2098.speech: Says she leaves "proud of the help the US has provided Ghana, beginning with the huge investment in construction of the Akosombo Dam"; states that US assistance evolved to include security cooperation valued now at over $25 million a year, that thanks to US provision of bed nets, malaria test kits and treatment the number of malaria deaths in Ghana dropped by two-thirds, that US-introduced higher-yield varieties of maize and soybeans increased productivity for 400,000 farmers, and that support for cashew, mango and shea crops drove $500 million in new agribusiness sales.

a2098.speaker: Virginia E. Palmer, US Ambassador to Ghana (2022-2025) (op-ed)
a2098.name: Virginia E. Palmer
a2098.title: US Ambassador to Ghana (2022-2025) (op-ed)
a2098.speech: Says that "Under President Trump, U.S. investment has evolved into focusing on commerce and engagement as an exchange between equals, echoing President Mahama's sentiment expressed in 2016"; and that President Mahama knows that to realise the full advantages of trade between equals requires investment in Ghana's youth and in education.

a2098.speaker: John Mahama, President of Ghana (quoted from 2016)
a2098.name: John Mahama
a2098.title: President of Ghana (quoted from 2016)
a2098.speech: "Africa does not need your sympathy or Overseas Development Assistance. Africa needs a fair chance to trade with the rest of the world and amongst ourselves."

a2098.speaker: Virginia E. Palmer, US Ambassador to Ghana (2022-2025) (op-ed)
a2098.name: Virginia E. Palmer
a2098.title: US Ambassador to Ghana (2022-2025) (op-ed)
a2098.speech: On security, argues that "Too many governments make the argument that democracy and free trade must wait for security. In fact, democracy and free trade strengthen security, as Ghana exemplifies to the world"; says Ghana exports peace through the thousands of Ghanaians who serve as UN peacekeepers, and that Ghana's commitment to inclusive economic growth, especially in Ghana's poorer North, bolstered by US support, makes Ghana resilient to violent extremism.

a2098.speaker: Virginia E. Palmer, US Ambassador to Ghana (2022-2025) (op-ed)
a2098.name: Virginia E. Palmer
a2098.title: US Ambassador to Ghana (2022-2025) (op-ed)
a2098.speech: Says "It has been an enormous privilege to serve as the US Ambassador to Ghana, and I am very honoured to end my nearly 40 years in the diplomatic service here. Ghana epitomises all the good the US can accomplish with strong partners who are leaders themselves" ; "And I am delighted now to become one of the millions of American citizens with a deep, personal tie to Ghana."

a2101.speaker: Military insiders (anonymous)
a2101.name: Military insiders (anonymous)
a2101.speech: Describe these vehicles as "death traps", posing a serious risk to the lives of Ghanaian soldiers deployed on international peacekeeping missions.

a2101.speaker: Technical reports and confidential military documents obtained by The Herald
a2101.name: Technical reports and confidential military documents obtained by The Herald
a2101.speech: Reveal that the APCs, now over 50 years old, are plagued with mechanical and structural deficiencies - oil and lubricant leakages, frequent engine overheating after limited use, malfunctioning brake and clutch systems, blurred vision blocks, missing side mirrors, and defective rear cameras - and that they lack intra- and inter-vehicle communication systems, leaving troops effectively isolated during operations.

a2101.speaker: Sources within the Ghana Army (anonymous)
a2101.name: Sources within the Ghana Army (anonymous)
a2101.speech: Describe the APCs as unfit for purpose; many arrived immobile and had to be transported from Tema Port to Burma Camp on low-loader trailers, and despite superficial refurbishment efforts most remain non-operational.

a2101.speaker: Soldiers who spoke to The Herald (anonymous)
a2101.name: Soldiers who spoke to The Herald (anonymous)
a2101.speech: Revealed that seven of the vehicles were shipped to Ghana's UN peacekeeping battalion in Abyei (UNISFA) in 2024.

a2101.speaker: Military mechanics (anonymous)
a2101.name: Military mechanics (anonymous)
a2101.speech: Report that while the original petrol engines of the BTR-70s were replaced with diesel variants, critical accompanying components such as radiators and hoses were not upgraded accordingly.

a2101.speaker: Insiders (anonymous)
a2101.name: Insiders (anonymous)
a2101.speech: Disclosed to The Herald that the APCs were effectively salvaged from a scrapyard in Azerbaijan.

a2101.speaker: Sources (anonymous)
a2101.name: Sources (anonymous)
a2101.speech: Further allege that Major General Thomas Oppong-Peprah, who served as Army Commander at the time and has since become CDS, was heavily involved in the transaction and is reported to have personally travelled to Azerbaijan alongside the suppliers to inspect and finalise the deal.

a2101.speaker: Confidential documents reviewed by The Herald
a2101.name: Confidential documents reviewed by The Herald
a2101.speech: Show that the GAF repeatedly sought waivers and expedited clearances to facilitate the vehicles' entry into Ghana; in letters addressed to Customs and Port Authorities dated between January and March 2023, military officers cited "budgetary constraints" and "urgent operational needs" to justify bypassing standard procedures.

a2101.speaker: Captain F.A. Amin, 1 Forces Movement Unit (memo)
a2101.name: Captain F.A. Amin
a2101.title: 1 Forces Movement Unit (memo)
a2101.speech: Requested a 100 percent waiver on state warehouse rent fees, citing an inability to pay GHS 4,800.

a2101.speaker: Captain E. Owusu-Acheampong (letter)
a2101.name: Captain E. Owusu-Acheampong (letter)
a2101.speech: Applied for release of the consignment before full customs processing was complete, stressing the "sensitive nature" of the shipment.

a2101.speaker: Defence analysts and military insiders
a2101.name: Defence analysts and military insiders
a2101.speech: Are now calling for a full value-for-money audit to assess the wisdom of the purchase and prevent similar embarrassments in future.

a2123.speaker: Dr Hussein Mwinyi, President of Zanzibar
a2123.name: Dr Hussein Mwinyi
a2123.title: President of Zanzibar
a2123.speech: Officially announced the dissolution of the 10th House of Representatives, effective August 13, 2025, to pave the way for the upcoming General Election, and noted that both the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and the Zanzibar Electoral Commission (ZEC) are actively preparing to ensure the successful conduct of the election.

a2123.speaker: Dr Hussein Mwinyi, President of Zanzibar
a2123.name: Dr Hussein Mwinyi
a2123.title: President of Zanzibar
a2123.speech: Reaffirmed his government's commitment to democracy and called on citizens to uphold peace: "Public participation in decision-making institutions is the cornerstone of democracy and good governance," saying that successive governments of the Zanzibar Revolutionary Government have consistently upheld this constitutional right ; praised the leadership, members and staff of the House for their dedication: "The effective functioning of this House has allowed it to advise the government, pass critical legislation and approve national budgets" ; noted parliamentary reforms including digitisation efforts that reduced the cost of printing official documents, and that by April 2025 the House had enacted or amended 44 laws.

a2123.speaker: Dr Hussein Mwinyi, President of Zanzibar
a2123.name: Dr Hussein Mwinyi
a2123.title: President of Zanzibar
a2123.speech: Said that Zanzibar's economy had shown impressive growth over the past five years, with GDP at current market prices rising from 4.78tri/- in 2021 to 6.57tri/- in 2024 - a 63 per cent increase, economic growth of 7.1 per cent in 2024, per capita income rising from 1,099 US dollars in 2020 to 1,395 US dollars in 2024, and government revenue collection increasing from 856bn/- in 2020/2021 to 2.104tri/- in 2023/2024.

a2123.speaker: Dr Hussein Mwinyi, President of Zanzibar
a2123.name: Dr Hussein Mwinyi
a2123.title: President of Zanzibar
a2123.speech: Said investment trends remained positive, with 485 projects worth 6.2 billion US dollars registered by June 2025, including 187 hotel-related projects, 112 commercial developments, 48 industrial ventures, 27 agricultural projects, 28 in sports and 83 in other sectors; added that Zanzibar is encouraging investment in its smaller islands, with the Zanzibar Investment Promotion Authority registering projects on 17 islands totalling 377.5 million US dollars.

a2123.speaker: Dr Hussein Mwinyi, President of Zanzibar
a2123.name: Dr Hussein Mwinyi
a2123.title: President of Zanzibar
a2123.speech: Said the eighth phase government has made significant strides in the blue economy, particularly in tourism, marine transport, fishing, seaweed farming, port development and oil and gas exploration, with tourist arrivals rising from 394,185 in 2021 to 736,755 in 2024, and said airport authority revenues rose from 12.9bn/- in 2021 to 40.2bn/- in 2025, a 211.6 per cent increase, with passenger numbers jumping from 840,559 in 2020 to 2,140,956 in 2025.

a2123.speaker: Dr Hussein Mwinyi, President of Zanzibar
a2123.name: Dr Hussein Mwinyi
a2123.title: President of Zanzibar
a2123.speech: Spoke on the Union, stating that political, economic and social relations have strengthened, that since the establishment of the Joint Union Affairs Committee in 2006, 26 Union matters have been discussed, 22 of which have been resolved, and said Zanzibar continues to benefit from the fair distribution of foreign aid and Union-initiated development projects.

a2214.speaker: European Parliament (resolution and statement)
a2214.name: European Parliament (resolution and statement)
a2214.speech: Urged the European Union to freeze direct budget support for Rwanda until it breaks links with Tutsi-led M23 rebels and allows humanitarian access to areas of the Democratic Republic of Congo where they advanced; also called for the suspension of a memorandum of understanding between Rwanda and the EU that aims to support Rwandan supplies of strategic minerals, until Rwanda stops interfering in Congo. "MEPs strongly condemn the occupation of Goma and other territories in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) by M23 rebels and the Rwandan defence forces as an (unacceptable) breach of the DRC's sovereignty and territorial integrity," the body said in a statement. The parliament adopted the resolution in a 443-4 vote, with another 48 lawmakers abstaining.

a2214.speaker: Yolande Makolo, Rwandan government spokesperson
a2214.name: Yolande Makolo
a2214.title: Rwandan government spokesperson
a2214.speech: Did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

a2214.speaker: Local official in eastern Congo (unnamed)
a2214.name: Local official in eastern Congo (unnamed)
a2214.speech: Has said the M23 advance threatens to trigger a humanitarian catastrophe in an area already housing thousands of displaced people.

a2214.speaker: Congo, the United Nations and several Western countries
a2214.name: Congo
a2214.title: the United Nations and several Western countries
a2214.speech: Have accused Rwanda of supporting M23 with its own troops and weapons.

a2214.speaker: Kigali (Rwandan government)
a2214.name: Kigali (Rwandan government)
a2214.speech: Denies the charge that it supports M23 with its own troops and weapons.

a2214.speaker: Igor Cesar, Rwandan ambassador to Belgium
a2214.name: Igor Cesar
a2214.title: Rwandan ambassador to Belgium
a2214.speech: In comments to a European Parliament panel on Thursday, said: "Rwanda is not the source of this conflict nor is it responsible for solving it alone."

a2217.speaker: Benedictus Freeman, USFS Liberia's country coordinator
a2217.name: Benedictus Freeman
a2217.title: USFS Liberia's country coordinator
a2217.speech: "The workshop contributes significantly to enhancing forest restoration efforts in Liberia" ; "By providing participants with the necessary knowledge and skills, the workshop has empowered them to play a vital role in restoring degraded lands in Liberia and promoting sustainable forest management."

a2217.speaker: Benedictus Freeman, USFS Liberia's country coordinator
a2217.name: Benedictus Freeman
a2217.title: USFS Liberia's country coordinator
a2217.speech: Said training laid the foundation for a potential collaboration between Guinea and Liberia, particularly in the Nimba landscape, and that the next steps would be to maintain the partnership with the FDA, ArcelorMittal and other participants.

a2217.speaker: Global Forest Watch
a2217.name: Global Forest Watch
a2217.speech: According to the Global Forest Watch, between 2001 and 2023 Liberia lost 2.36 million hectares of tree cover, 17 hectares from fire.

a2217.speaker: Experts
a2217.name: Experts
a2217.speech: Say harmful farming methods, logging, and mining are the key drivers of deforestation and forest degradation in Liberia.

a2217.speaker: Alphonso Kiedor, FDA's restoration manager
a2217.name: Alphonso Kiedor
a2217.title: FDA's restoration manager
a2217.speech: "It means a lot to me. All the people who participated will be able to apply the knowledge in their communities" ; "It will transform our learning field as well. I am sure that we are going to make a great change."

a2958.speaker: Cocoa Barometer report, produced by the VOICE Network group of civil society organisations
a2958.name: Cocoa Barometer report
a2958.title: produced by the VOICE Network group of civil society organisations
a2958.speech: According to the report, Ivory Coast was able to trace about 40% of its beans in the 2024-25 (October to September) season.

a2958.speaker: Antonie Fountain, VOICE Network director
a2958.name: Antonie Fountain
a2958.title: VOICE Network director
a2958.speech: Told Reuters the country would be able to trace far more beans this season; he also stressed that the only way to ensure full compliance was for the law to come into effect.

a2958.speaker: Antonie Fountain and co-author Friedel Huetz-Adams (Cocoa Barometer report)
a2958.name: Antonie Fountain and co-author Friedel Huetz-Adams (Cocoa Barometer report)
a2958.speech: “While virtually all cocoa stakeholders, including industry, seemed to be aligned, a political shift to the right has caused a sudden slashing of funding for sustainability worldwide” ; “The regulatory unreliability of the EU is causing severe damage to planetary protection.”

a2958.speaker: Ivory Coast (government)
a2958.name: Ivory Coast (government)
a2958.speech: Says around 900,000 of 1 million cocoa farmers have received their digital ID cards.

a2958.speaker: United States (as an EU trade partner)
a2958.name: United States (as an EU trade partner)
a2958.speech: Said complying with the rules would be costly.

a3007.speaker: Chief Matipa of the Bisa people, traditional leader
a3007.name: Chief Matipa of the Bisa people
a3007.title: traditional leader
a3007.speech: Said it was important for investors to employ local people and to help develop his chiefdom; said he could not allow investors to bring in expatriates when the locals were able to do the work ; "I want my people to benefit from the investment being brought in the chiefdom. I want to see my people's welfare change" ; said he was open to work with investors that would enhance economic activities in his chiefdom and that he wants to see to it that the welfare of the people in the area improves.

a3007.speaker: Wang Haipeng, vice president of the China Asia Economic Development Association
a3007.name: Wang Haipeng
a3007.title: vice president of the China Asia Economic Development Association
a3007.speech: Said the cassava processing plant will have the capacity to process 100,000 metric tonnes of cassava for export.

a3075.speaker: Nathan Sage, USAID/Tanzania Environment Team Lead
a3075.name: Nathan Sage
a3075.title: USAID/Tanzania Environment Team Lead
a3075.speech: “Balancing the well-being of humans and wildlife using finite resources is a complex challenge, requiring inclusive and collaborative solutions. USAID’s work in conservation is grounded in elevating community involvement in and ownership of land-use planning” ; “The United States believes it is essential that designated corridors are based on village land-use plans including existing grazing rights, provided that there are sustainable management plans and that these village plans are recognised and upheld so that communities retain ownership and control over corridor area natural resources.”

a3075.speaker: Zakaria Faustin, Executive Director of the Tanzania Natural Resources Forum
a3075.name: Zakaria Faustin
a3075.title: Executive Director of the Tanzania Natural Resources Forum
a3075.speech: “securing landscape connectivity may involve more than one village and requires a community-driven process where the community becomes the centre of the process. The community should be well-informed to make decisions about the use of their land through joint land use plans. We tried that in Kiteto, and it worked. The community supported the work because they have seen a tangible benefit.”

a3075.speaker: USAID/Tanzania
a3075.name: USAID/Tanzania
a3075.speech: Is committed to supporting wildlife corridor guidelines that protect community land and grazing rights, in line with international best practices such as Free, Prior and Informed Consent.

a3147.speaker: Bola Tinubu, President of Nigeria
a3147.name: Bola Tinubu
a3147.title: President of Nigeria
a3147.speech: Has directed the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) to return the food items seized at border communities to the rightful owners, with the caveat that the owners must be willing to sell the items in Nigerian markets.

a3147.speaker: Adewale Adeniyi, Comptroller General of Customs
a3147.name: Adewale Adeniyi
a3147.title: Comptroller General of Customs
a3147.speech: Said that President Tinubu chose to exercise his authority not based on legal criteria, but rather out of a genuine sense of goodwill towards Nigeria ; “In doing so, he has directed that those food items that were going out of the country that have been seized in various border areas should be returned to the owners on the condition that those goods would be sold in the Nigerian markets.” ; “So, we will be monitoring you to know if there is a violation of this. Those food items will be returned, and it is a directive that we will pass them back into the Nigerian markets.”

a3147.speaker: Adewale Adeniyi, Comptroller General of Customs
a3147.name: Adewale Adeniyi
a3147.title: Comptroller General of Customs
a3147.speech: Revealed that President Tinubu will choose to reopen borders very soon and confirmed that the Service will prioritise eliminating barriers that hinder free trade ; “We are conscious of the concerns of the border communities, particularly with regards to the number of checkpoints and the closure of land borders. I assure you that our operations are always guided by law, and we only operate on delegated powers. We have communicated the concerns and complaints by residents of the border communities to the President and because he has listening ears, he directed that we should release confiscated food items, on the condition that they will only be sold in the Nigerian markets.” ; “We know that there are markets around our borders, and we know that not all of them are targeted at taking goods across the borders. We will continue to monitor and ensure that food produced in Nigeria remains and is consumed in Nigeria. This is because we are in a period of national emergency that has to do with food insufficiency. And that is why we must collectively work together to assist the government to enforce the various laws prohibiting exportation of food items at this time.”

a3147.speaker: The Sun News (report)
a3147.name: The Sun News (report)
a3147.speech: The SunNews reports that President Tinubu chose to exercise his authority not based on legal criteria, but rather out of a genuine sense of goodwill towards Nigeria.

a3322.speaker: Proponents of the Startup Act
a3322.name: Proponents of the Startup Act
a3322.speech: Argue that early-stage seed funding will help unlock entrepreneurship across the country.

a3322.speaker: The authorities (Ministry of Innovation & Technology / government)
a3322.name: The authorities (Ministry of Innovation & Technology / government)
a3322.speech: Believe the Council can be a vehicle to mobilise resources from the public and the private sectors, including equity firms.

a3322.speaker: Cepheus Research & Analytics (report on Ethiopia’s digital economy)
a3322.name: Cepheus Research & Analytics (report on Ethiopia’s digital economy)
a3322.speech: Showed that banks handle over a quarter of a trillion Birr annually in transactions value through digital channels, and Ethio telecom is advancing its customers 1.1 billion Br worth of airtime loans each month; the taxi-hailing industry is estimated to be providing 90,000 rides every day.

a3322.speaker: Ministry of Civil Service (then)
a3322.name: Ministry of Civil Service (then)
a3322.speech: The Civil Service Reform Program had aimed to improve “effectiveness, efficiency and ethical behaviour in performance and service delivery,” according to the then Ministry of Civil Service.

a3357.speaker: Resolution signed by 47 lawmakers of the Liberian House of Representatives, October 17
a3357.name: Resolution signed by 47 lawmakers of the Liberian House of Representatives
a3357.title: October 17
a3357.speech: Calls for Speaker Koffa's removal, claiming he no longer enjoys their confidence.

a3357.speaker: The rebellious/renegade lawmakers of the House of Representatives
a3357.name: The rebellious/renegade lawmakers of the House of Representatives
a3357.speech: Accuse him of manipulating the House budget and using his position to further his personal business interests, which they argue undermines his leadership and the integrity of the legislative body. They are yet to prove their allegations against their leader.

a3357.speaker: Supporters of Speaker J. Fonati Koffa
a3357.name: Supporters of Speaker J. Fonati Koffa
a3357.speech: Counter that the move to oust him is driven by an audit he initiated, which is likely to expose significant financial misconduct implicating several high-ranking members of the Legislature — possibly including himself ; further allege that the 'majority bloc' is keen to prevent Speaker Koffa from presiding over the 2025 Budget hearing, which could potentially allow them to manipulate the budget.

a3357.speaker: J. Fonati Koffa, Speaker of the Liberian House of Representatives
a3357.name: J. Fonati Koffa
a3357.title: Speaker of the Liberian House of Representatives
a3357.speech: Vowed not to bow to old tactics or maneuvers that saw the removals of former Speakers; according to him, resigning or stepping down is not an option and he will ensure the law is followed to the letter ; said on Capitol Hill on Tuesday, October 22, that he can only be removed, constitutionally, for a cause by resolution of a two-thirds majority of the members of the House, as enshrined in Article 49.

a3357.speaker: Speaker J. Fonati Koffa and his team
a3357.name: Speaker J. Fonati Koffa and his team
a3357.speech: Reaffirmed their commitment to working in the interest of the Liberian people and urged all members to uphold their responsibilities diligently.

a3357.speaker: Thomas Fallah, Deputy Speaker of the Liberian House of Representatives
a3357.name: Thomas Fallah
a3357.title: Deputy Speaker of the Liberian House of Representatives
a3357.speech: Accused of co-masterminding the plan to remove Speaker Koffa, he remained silent during the proceedings (no comment).

a3357.speaker: Some lawmakers of the House of Representatives
a3357.name: Some lawmakers of the House of Representatives
a3357.speech: Have vowed to put their political careers on the line to ensure that such a form of political dark act is discouraged and erased from the Liberian political landscape.

a3357.speaker: Musa Hassan Bility, Nimba County District #7 Representative
a3357.name: Musa Hassan Bility
a3357.title: Nimba County District #7 Representative
a3357.speech: "We are fully aware of your history of coercing speakers to resign, but that ends here. If you intend to oust Fonati Koffa as Speaker, you will need to rally 49 or more lawmakers in the House of Representatives to legitimately exercise their authority for his removal. Any actions taken without this majority will merely serve to inflate your egos." ; "In the past, your tactics may have succeeded because there were few willing to stand against you. However, today, we have courageous individuals ready to hold you accountable and demand respect for the rule of law. Remember: THE LAW IS THE LAW."

a3357.speaker: U.S. Ambassador to Liberia
a3357.name: U.S. Ambassador to Liberia
a3357.speech: Recently met with Speaker Koffa, calling for both parties to seek resolution through dialogue, cautioning that ongoing discord may jeopardize foreign aid and investment.

a3376.speaker: Ornella Tchuente, image and influence strategist, founder of the Indice d’Influence Africaine™
a3376.name: Ornella Tchuente
a3376.title: image and influence strategist, founder of the Indice d’Influence Africaine™
a3376.speech: Said on what motivated the Index: “My vision is clear: to build an elite of ethical and strategic influencers who, through their stance, their choices and their legacy, transform the perception and the place of Africa in the world. I refuse to have our African models read through outside prisms that minimise or distort their influence. I therefore created the Indice d’Influence Africaine™, an unprecedented methodology that makes it possible to measure influence in a rooted way.”

a3376.speaker: Ornella Tchuente, founder of the Indice d’Influence Africaine™
a3376.name: Ornella Tchuente
a3376.title: founder of the Indice d’Influence Africaine™
a3376.speech: Said Patrice Talon perfectly illustrates the figure of the president-entrepreneur because he first built his legitimacy through the economy before translating it into the exercise of political power, starting from cotton and building an empire that earned him the nickname “King of Cotton” ; said what distinguishes him is his capacity to apply the reflexes of the entrepreneur to governance, a style that “can be described as a ‘dictatorship of efficiency’: few populist speeches, a great deal of rigour in the follow-up of projects”, making him not the archetype of the traditional politician but “an architect of development” ; said he embodies a generation of African leaders who demonstrate that one can move from business to the public sphere without renouncing one’s codes.

a3376.speaker: Ornella Tchuente, founder of the Indice d’Influence Africaine™
a3376.name: Ornella Tchuente
a3376.title: founder of the Indice d’Influence Africaine™
a3376.speech: Said the Index distinguishes itself from traditional rankings because it does not stop at visibility or digital popularity, and rests on five cultural and strategic dimensions: silent authority, deliberate legacy, selective radiance, temporal transcendence and symbolic density: “the Index does not ask: ‘Who makes the most noise?’ It answers rather the question: ‘Who will leave a lasting, coherent and respected trace?’”

a3376.speaker: Ornella Tchuente, founder of the Indice d’Influence Africaine™
a3376.name: Ornella Tchuente
a3376.title: founder of the Indice d’Influence Africaine™
a3376.speech: Said economic growth expressed solely in figures can give a flattering but incomplete image — a country can post +6% of GDP, but if this does not translate into inclusion, productivity and equitable redistribution its impact remains limited ; said that in the case of Benin growth is undeniable but the challenge is now to transform this performance into inclusive growth: strengthening education and access to opportunities for young people, improving agricultural and industrial productivity so as not to depend solely on services or cotton, and ensuring that women, rural communities and the middle classes benefit directly.

a3376.speaker: World Bank (cited)
a3376.name: World Bank (cited)
a3376.speech: Points to the challenges of productivity and inclusion despite Benin’s sustained growth.

a3376.speaker: Ornella Tchuente, founder of the Indice d’Influence Africaine™
a3376.name: Ornella Tchuente
a3376.title: founder of the Indice d’Influence Africaine™
a3376.speech: Said of Vision 2060 Alafia that “an announcement captivates the moment, but a vision captivates generations”, and that the project goes beyond an announcement effect through its symbolic coherence (the Yoruba word “Alafia”, meaning peace and prosperity), its institutional architecture of programmes, infrastructure and measurable monitoring frameworks, and its generational projection ; said it “has already crossed an important threshold: it has created a collective hope.”

a3376.speaker: Ornella Tchuente, founder of the Indice d’Influence Africaine™
a3376.name: Ornella Tchuente
a3376.title: founder of the Indice d’Influence Africaine™
a3376.speech: Said that for the Glo-Djigbé Industrial Zone (Gdiz) the official figures speak for themselves, but that beyond statistics her analytical grid rests on the quality of the jobs, the durability of the ecosystem and citizen perception, and that she looks at both the symbolic effect (whether the Gdiz becomes a marker of national pride and continental radiance) and the lived effect (whether populations recognise themselves in the project or perceive it as a distant showcase).

a3376.speaker: Beninese authorities (official figures, cited)
a3376.name: Beninese authorities (official figures
a3376.title: cited)
a3376.speech: According to the authorities, more than 10,000 direct jobs have been created at the Glo-Djigbé Industrial Zone, with an integrated textile factory of world dimension being finalised and concrete exports already, including Made in Benin garments sent to U.S. Polo Assn. and 80,000 pieces delivered to Kiabi.

a3376.speaker: Ornella Tchuente, founder of the Indice d’Influence Africaine™
a3376.name: Ornella Tchuente
a3376.title: founder of the Indice d’Influence Africaine™
a3376.speech: Said the Port of Cotonou is the economic lung of Benin, responsible for nearly 90% of external trade and contributing more than half of national GDP, and that the African Development Bank’s validation in February 2025 of 80 million euros of financing shows the infrastructure is perceived as strategic regionally and internationally ; said it has become an indispensable regional platform for landlocked countries such as Niger, Burkina Faso and Mali and is an example of selective radiance and temporal transcendence ; said its 660-metre perimeter fresco, already considered the longest in the world, transforms an economic infrastructure into a cultural symbol projecting openness, pride and creativity.

a3376.speaker: Ornella Tchuente, founder of the Indice d’Influence Africaine™
a3376.name: Ornella Tchuente
a3376.title: founder of the Indice d’Influence Africaine™
a3376.speech: Said that on social media the question of radiance is not reduced to a contest of figures and that selective radiance measures relevance rather than mass — the quality of interactions, the capacity to dominate certain targeted spaces and the coherence between message and audience ; said she does not have access to the precise statistics of President Talon’s social networks but that he does not seek to be omnipresent or saturate the digital space, which “creates an effect of rarity and weight.”

a3376.speaker: Ornella Tchuente, founder of the Indice d’Influence Africaine™
a3376.name: Ornella Tchuente
a3376.title: founder of the Indice d’Influence Africaine™
a3376.speech: Said she is above all an observer and strategist, not a master of universal solutions, and that the “Beninese model” is not a scheme to be copied identically but a prism of reflection applicable elsewhere ; named three transferable aspects — a generational vision beyond the political cycle (observed also in Kigali, planning beyond 2040, and Lagos), integrated infrastructure serving sub-regional influence such as the Port of Cotonou, and a symbolic and coherent leadership combining efficiency and local storytelling.

a3376.speaker: Ornella Tchuente, founder of the Indice d’Influence Africaine™
a3376.name: Ornella Tchuente
a3376.title: founder of the Indice d’Influence Africaine™
a3376.speech: Said the resilience of a political system is measured in its capacity to continue functioning when a leader withdraws, and that Talon’s categorical refusal of a third term, confirmed on several occasions in 2025, inscribes his influence in an institutional dynamic rather than a logic of personal power.

a3376.speaker: Ornella Tchuente, founder of the Indice d’Influence Africaine™
a3376.name: Ornella Tchuente
a3376.title: founder of the Indice d’Influence Africaine™
a3376.speech: “For me, Patrice Talon embodies the silent authority that builds a lasting legacy. He did not seek to seduce through noise, but to transform through structure, leaving a trace that goes beyond his mandate and is already inscribed in the history of Benin and of Africa.”

a3376.speaker: Patrice Talon, President of Benin
a3376.name: Patrice Talon
a3376.title: President of Benin
a3376.speech: Announced that he would not seek a third term, a refusal confirmed on several occasions in 2025.

a3453.speaker: Dr Mutumwa Muyangana, Medical Officer for the USAID TB LON project (CIDRZ)
a3453.name: Dr Mutumwa Muyangana
a3453.title: Medical Officer for the USAID TB LON project (CIDRZ)
a3453.speech: Said the 10 oxygen concentrators would improve patient care at the UTH-Children's Hospital: "The USAID TB LON project, implemented by CIDRZ, has been working closely with both the Children's Hospital and the Adult Hospital. I am delighted to hand over these oxygen concentrators as part of our ongoing support to the hospital" ; said the donation shows the strong partnership between CIDRZ, the Ministry of Health, and UTH's management and staff: "This collaboration ensures that the patients, both children and adults, receive the best possible care" ; "We are honoured to be able to contribute to this effort and look forward to continuing our support to strengthen healthcare in Zambia."

a3453.speaker: Dr Mutumwa Muyangana, Medical Officer for the USAID TB LON project (CIDRZ)
a3453.name: Dr Mutumwa Muyangana
a3453.title: Medical Officer for the USAID TB LON project (CIDRZ)
a3453.speech: Said the TB LON Project had been instrumental in supporting tuberculosis patients in tertiary hospitals across eight provinces, and explained that many patients who sought treatment at such hospitals presented more complex forms of TB, which often required respiratory support: "In some cases, patients require respiratory support even after completing TB treatment, due to complications arising from the disease itself. This highlights the need for advanced approaches in patient management, including the use of oxygen therapy" ; "We are confident that these concentrators will be put to good use, ensuring that patients in need of oxygen therapy can receive it promptly and effectively."

a3507.speaker: Mulu Nega, CEO of the Tigray Interim Administration
a3507.name: Mulu Nega
a3507.title: CEO of the Tigray Interim Administration
a3507.speech: Said the relief and the emergency activities managed by the Tigray Interim Administration is going well despite the rampant baseless disinformation ; said his administration is progressing well to achieve all the priorities set in the short and long term plans of the region ; stressed that there is very huge demand in humanitarian assistance, but “the relief and the emergency activities are going well in the region” ; stated that the administration “has already started providing food for the needy population at all levels, and we have agreed with the responsible federal government sectors to speed up and strengthen the activities because people should get food and all basic necessities” ; said the only thing that needs to be strengthened is the distribution to all woredas and cities as the flow is very good, adding that this is also going well but will be strengthened to address all the population in the region.

a3534.speaker: Chief Olusegun Obasanjo, Chairman of the IATF2025 Advisory Council and former Nigerian President
a3534.name: Chief Olusegun Obasanjo
a3534.title: Chairman of the IATF2025 Advisory Council and former Nigerian President
a3534.speech: Addressing the opening ceremony, described the fair as a symbol of Africa’s economic awakening; noted that the event has become a major platform for connecting buyers, sellers, investors and governments from across the continent; reported that 48 African countries are participating in exhibitions, marking the largest country participation since the inaugural fair in 2018; highlighted the fair’s record of facilitating major deals, stating that the previous three editions had generated combined trade and investment commitments exceeding R2.2-trillion; pointed to the Julius Nyerere Hydropower Project in Tanzania, a R54-billion deal signed at the 2018 fair, as an example of the transformational deals the event enables.

a3534.speaker: Ambassador Selma Malika Haddadi, African Union Commission Deputy Chairperson
a3534.name: Ambassador Selma Malika Haddadi
a3534.title: African Union Commission Deputy Chairperson
a3534.speech: Echoed this sentiment, noting that each edition of the fair has brought the continent closer to the goals of the African Union’s Agenda 2063; stated that boosting intra-African trade is both an economic and political imperative, noting that while Africa contributes only 2.9 per cent to global trade, intra-African trade has been growing, expanding by 27 per cent between 2017 and 2023 to approach R3.7 trillion; pointed to the fact that trade between African countries is primarily driven by manufactured goods, which account for 45 per cent of intra-African commerce, compared to just 20 per cent of the continent’s exports outside Africa.

a3534.speaker: Ambassador Selma Malika Haddadi, African Union Commission Deputy Chairperson
a3534.name: Ambassador Selma Malika Haddadi
a3534.title: African Union Commission Deputy Chairperson
a3534.speech: Was frank about the challenges, noting that intra-African trade still represents a mere 15 per cent of total African trade; identified systemic barriers, including costly trade restrictions, fragmented infrastructure and financial systems that do not connect, which make trading with a neighbour more difficult than trading abroad.

a3534.speaker: Mike Whitfield, Stellantis South African and sub-Saharan African head
a3534.name: Mike Whitfield
a3534.title: Stellantis South African and sub-Saharan African head
a3534.speech: Announced at a recent Stellantis event in Johannesburg that proper implementation of the AfCFTA combined with the growing number of automotive assembly plants in Africa could see countries – including South Africa – importing vehicles from within Africa in the near future.

a3534.speaker: Wamkele Mene, Secretary General of the AfCFTA Secretariat
a3534.name: Wamkele Mene
a3534.title: Secretary General of the AfCFTA Secretariat
a3534.speech: “The AfCFTA is already delivering. Intra-African trade rebounded strongly in 2024, recording a 12.4 per cent increase from 2023, according to Afreximbank’s African Trade Report 2025. This recovery underscores growing confidence in Africa’s integration model under the AfCFTA. Beyond the headline figures, the data shows a gradual shift in the continent’s trade composition. While primary commodities still dominate, there is a clear growth in machinery, motor vehicles, food products, chemicals and electronics. This shift signals our continent’s transition from raw commodity dependency toward industrial diversification, a shift that will only be sustained by stronger logistics and manufacturing value chains.”

a3579.speaker: MCC executive (at a staff meeting)
a3579.name: MCC executive (at a staff meeting)
a3579.speech: Told staff that “we are coming to an orderly close” with all programs to be discontinued, according to an employee who was present.

a3579.speaker: MCC staff-wide memo (seen by AFP)
a3579.name: MCC staff-wide memo (seen by AFP)
a3579.speech: Informed that billionaire Elon Musk's Department of Government Efficiency was imposing a “significant reduction” at MCC and laid out practicalities for the majority of staff who will lose jobs.

a3579.speaker: Hakainde Hichilema, Zambian President
a3579.name: Hakainde Hichilema
a3579.title: Zambian President
a3579.speech: Just in October, vowed to keep upholding “shared values” with the United States as he signed a half-billion-dollar agreement to improve roads, irrigation and electricity.

a3579.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3579.name: Donald Trump
a3579.title: US President
a3579.speech: Has made clear he has limited interest in sub-Saharan Africa and that he opposes development aid, which he sees as not directly benefiting the United States.

a3579.speaker: MCC employee (anonymous, speaking on condition of anonymity to avoid retribution)
a3579.name: MCC employee (anonymous
a3579.title: speaking on condition of anonymity to avoid retribution)
a3579.speech: Said the organization differed significantly from USAID: “We're not doing humanitarian assistance. We're not doing social justice. We're very much building up an environment for private-sector investment in foreign economies” ; “This is a very different thing, something that actually does put America first” ; “It's interesting, if we're worried about China's influence in the world, that we would shutter MCC, which builds large-scale infrastructure that counters China's influence.”

a3579.speaker: MCC employee (anonymous, speaking on condition of anonymity to avoid retribution)
a3579.name: MCC employee (anonymous
a3579.title: speaking on condition of anonymity to avoid retribution)
a3579.speech: Said MCC will inform countries on Friday that compacts will be terminated within 40 days; that after negotiations with Musk's team, MCC was allowed extensions in four countries – Ivory Coast, Mongolia, Nepal and Senegal – with up to three months in Nepal, Mongolia and Senegal, with hopes of making construction sites safe. The goal is “so someone is not going to fall into a pit or something... Whether or not we'll be successful, I don't know.”

a3579.speaker: Xi Jinping, Chinese President
a3579.name: Xi Jinping
a3579.title: Chinese President
a3579.speech: In September vowed another $51 billion of investment in Africa over the next three years.

a3579.speaker: United States under former president Joe Biden
a3579.name: United States under former president Joe Biden
a3579.speech: Acknowledged it cannot keep up with such high-profile, state-led spending but argued it can offer a more sustainable model.

a3579.speaker: Elizabeth Hoffman, executive director for North America at ONE, the anti-poverty group co-founded by Bono
a3579.name: Elizabeth Hoffman
a3579.title: executive director for North America at ONE, the anti-poverty group co-founded by Bono
a3579.speech: Voiced alarm at the shutdown: “MCC brings an innovative and entrepreneurial approach to development assistance that holds governments accountable and effectively counters malign foreign influences like China.”

a3579.speaker: MCC and Trump administration (non-response)
a3579.name: MCC and Trump administration (non-response)
a3579.speech: MCC and Trump administration did not immediately comment on the cuts, which were first reported by development specialist site Devex.

a3579.speaker: Devex (development specialist site)
a3579.name: Devex (development specialist site)
a3579.speech: First reported the cuts at MCC.

a3674.speaker: Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh, President of the Djibouti Chamber of Commerce
a3674.name: Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh
a3674.title: President of the Djibouti Chamber of Commerce
a3674.speech: Said in a speech at the ceremony that the funding mobilised under this project had made it possible to train young jobseekers in trades consistent with Djibouti's vision of economic development, namely transport and port logistics ; “To that end, a framework agreement has been signed between the Centre for Resources and Skills and EDC/USAID, in order to train 400 young jobseekers in port, transport and logistics trades, so as to meet the needs of the labour market,” he added, before urging companies operating in this field to get in touch with the CRC to learn about the skills of the young people trained to internationally recognised standards.

a3674.speaker: Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh, President of the Djibouti Chamber of Commerce
a3674.name: Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh
a3674.title: President of the Djibouti Chamber of Commerce
a3674.speech: “The Djibouti Chamber of Commerce wanted to create synergies among the projects in which it is involved”: said the Chamber, as representative of the private sector, is a stakeholder in the project alongside the Ministry of Labour (through ANEFIP), the Ministry of National Education and the Ministry of Transport; that trainees are to be trained on articulated and rigid vehicles, public transport buses, RTGs, RSs, gantry cranes and forklifts; that 100 people have been trained to date (78 for articulated vehicles with category E licences, 22 for rigid vehicles with category C licences); and that the Chamber faces difficulty mobilising enough candidates holding category E licences and has approached several partners to make it easier for unemployed young people to obtain them.

a3674.speaker: Larry E. Andre, United States Ambassador to Djibouti
a3674.name: Larry E. Andre
a3674.title: United States Ambassador to Djibouti
a3674.speech: Indicated that the tripartite partnership between the CCD, the AFD and USAID had resulted in high-level training in transport and logistics for insufficiently schooled young people, who he said represent a large share of young jobseekers ; “I take this opportunity to assure you of the readiness of the American people, through USAID, to continue financing 50% of the cost of the training until the target of 400 young people is reached under this partnership,” he told his partners.

a3674.speaker: Larry E. Andre, United States Ambassador to Djibouti
a3674.name: Larry E. Andre
a3674.title: United States Ambassador to Djibouti
a3674.speech: “The US government renews its commitment to support Djibouti in its efforts to develop human capital within the framework of Vision 2035”: said the training was made possible by the tripartite partnership between the Djibouti Chamber of Commerce, the AFD and USAID, which responds to growing private-sector demand for qualified personnel and supports government efforts to create jobs and promote the hiring of young people and women in logistics and transport; said Djibouti faces the twin challenges of a lack of qualified candidates for available technical posts and a lack of hiring opportunities for young people and women, and that technical training addresses both.

a3674.speaker: Laura Dillon-Binkley, Head of USAID's “Education Development Center” project
a3674.name: Laura Dillon-Binkley
a3674.title: Head of USAID's “Education Development Center” project
