a3674.speech: “The CRC will provide training for qualified Djiboutian jobseekers who can successfully enter employment” ; “I want to thank the chamber of commerce and all the donors, the European Union, the French Development Agency, USAID and the American government for the establishment of this centre, which is truly of capital importance for Djibouti with regard to technical training in port trades. Because we know that there is a mismatch between the profile sought by employers in the ports and the availability on the market of qualified people. And this training centre will fill that gap and ensure that we have Djiboutian jobseekers who are qualified and who can successfully enter employment.”

a3674.speaker: Mohamed Ahmed Houssein, beneficiary of the training
a3674.name: Mohamed Ahmed Houssein
a3674.title: beneficiary of the training
a3674.speech: “Despite my years of experience as a truck driver, previously I could not meet the requirements of the international companies that operate in our various port facilities. This training helped me improve and master the driving of all types of vehicles. These 4 weeks of training helped me learn a great deal about interpersonal communication, being proactive in any given situation and working in a spirit of teamwork with one's colleagues. With the certificate I received today, I will find a well-paid job. I take this opportunity to thank the CRC, the EDC, the AFD, USAID and the CCD. I also thank the President of the Republic Ismail Omar Guelleh and the First Lady Kadra Mahamoud Haid for her policy of developing human capital, which allowed us to take part in this training which will certainly raise our standard of living.”

a3674.speaker: Designers of the Djibouti Workforce Employability Project (PED)
a3674.name: Designers of the Djibouti Workforce Employability Project (PED)
a3674.speech: According to its designers, the PED — a five-year project financed by the United States government through USAID — aims to improve the skills and competitiveness of Djiboutian jobseekers in line with international standards.

a3685.speaker: Mwigulu Nchemba, Tanzanian Finance Minister
a3685.name: Mwigulu Nchemba
a3685.title: Tanzanian Finance Minister
a3685.speech: Informed the National Assembly that 88bn/- of the funds have already been disbursed to ensure the continuation of key health projects impacted by the policy changes ; clarified that Tanzania had no direct government-to-government financial cooperation with the US for development project funding, and that instead most US development assistance was channelled through American institutions working with Tanzanian partners ; “There was no direct budgetary impact following the foreign aid policy changes,” he said, adding, “However, the government conducted a thorough assessment of institutions previously receiving such funds — not only in response to the US policy shift but as part of a broader review of support from development partners.” ; said the government is committed to ensuring continuity of the affected projects, especially in the health sector, by allocating necessary funds from its own budget and other sources.

a3685.speaker: Mwigulu Nchemba, Tanzanian Finance Minister
a3685.name: Mwigulu Nchemba
a3685.title: Tanzanian Finance Minister
a3685.speech: Said the government is intensifying efforts to operationalise major domestic projects that rely on locally available resources to boost domestic revenue and reduce reliance on imported goods ; “These initiatives will not only generate substantial income but also increase the production of goods that can be made locally, enhancing economic resilience,” he noted ; said Tanzania is scaling up efforts to increase domestic revenue generation, aiming to finance a significant portion of the national budget internally, and added that the government will continue to attract private sector participation in development financing through public-private partnerships (PPPs) and other innovative models ; “This strategy will help reduce the borrowing burden on the government and lessen budgetary dependence on development partners,” he said.

a3685.speaker: Patrick Ndakidemi (CCM), MP for Moshi Rural
a3685.name: Patrick Ndakidemi (CCM)
a3685.title: MP for Moshi Rural
a3685.speech: Asked a supplementary question inquiring about the effect of a recent executive order by former US President Donald Trump on development initiatives in Tanzania and how the country plans to utilise its natural resources to mitigate such external shocks, and a primary question on the government’s preparedness to counter foreign policy shifts from developed nations.

a3718.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP/PAM)
a3718.name: World Food Programme (WFP/PAM)
a3718.speech: Announced on Friday that it was suspending its food and nutrition aid in crisis-affected countries of West and Central Africa because of US aid cuts, which is paralysing the organisation’s operations ; said that although timelines vary, food stocks should last until around September for most of the countries concerned, potentially leaving millions of vulnerable people without any emergency assistance ; said aid distribution has already been considerably reduced in Cameroonian camps hosting Nigerian refugees ; said it needs $494 million to cover the second half of 2025, but funds are completely exhausted, forcing it to prioritise the most vulnerable groups, and that in northern and central Mali it will prioritise newly displaced refugees and children under five.

a3718.speaker: Margot van der Velden, WFP Regional Director
a3718.name: Margot van der Velden
a3718.title: WFP Regional Director
a3718.speech: Told the Associated Press: “We are doing everything we can to prioritise the most life-saving activities, but without urgent support from our partners, our response capacity diminishes every day. We need sustainable funding to maintain the food supply and keep hope alive.”

a3718.speaker: WFP data consulted by the Associated Press
a3718.name: WFP data consulted by the Associated Press
a3718.speech: Showed that millions of people are expected to be immediately affected, including 300,000 children in Nigeria at risk of “severe malnutrition, ultimately increasing the risk of death.”

a3763.speaker: Stakeholders at the Youth and Society (YAS) seminar (lawyers, economists and governance commentators)
a3763.name: Stakeholders at the Youth and Society (YAS) seminar (lawyers
a3763.title: economists and governance commentators)
a3763.speech: Said there is need for detailed regulation on how the DPP exercises power.

a3763.speaker: Tusume Mwabungulu, Malawi Law Society (MLS) vice-president
a3763.name: Tusume Mwabungulu
a3763.title: Malawi Law Society (MLS) vice-president
a3763.speech: Proposed that the DPP's decisions to discontinue cases must be reviewed by the courts: "DPPs reasons for exercise of powers must be reviewable by the courts. There must be more transparency and accountability." ; Said there is need to develop detailed regulations on how to exercise these powers to allay public fears on what considerations have been made.

a3763.speaker: Bertha Bangara-Chikadza, University of Malawi economist and Economists Association of Malawi president
a3763.name: Bertha Bangara-Chikadza
a3763.title: University of Malawi economist and Economists Association of Malawi president
a3763.speech: Said the exercise of power for this office can boost or kill the economy: "In cases involving cross-border crimes such as money laundering, human trafficking, or cybercrime, the DPP's actions can have international economic implications. Cooperation with foreign jurisdictions and adherence to global standards can enhance a country's reputation and attract foreign investment." ; Added that failure to prosecute such crimes effectively may "lead to sanctions, reduced foreign aid, or exclusion from international financial systems", all of which may hurt the economy.

a3763.speaker: Benedicto Kondowe, activist, and Ernest Thindwa, political scientist (joint paper)
a3763.name: Benedicto Kondowe
a3763.title: activist, and Ernest Thindwa, political scientist (joint paper)
a3763.speech: Recommended the establishment of a prosecutorial oversight committee within Parliament that should periodically review the DPP's performance ; proposed strengthening the parliamentary Legal Affairs Committee's oversight mandate to scrutinise the basis of discontinuance beyond merely providing reasons as required under Section 99 of the Constitution.

a3763.speaker: Charles Kajoloweka, YAS executive director
a3763.name: Charles Kajoloweka
a3763.title: YAS executive director
a3763.speech: Said the DPP sits at the heart of the justice system, hence the need for improved accountability: "But history has shown that this office, like many others, is not immune to political pressure, resource constraints, and systemic inefficiencies. The question we must answer today is: how do we transform the DPP's mandate into a beacon of accountability rather than an instrument of political convenience?" ; Said they will compile the suggestions from the seminar and present them to authorities for consideration.

a3763.speaker: Masauko Chamkakala, Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP)
a3763.name: Masauko Chamkakala
a3763.title: Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP)
a3763.speech: Responding to the concerns, said the office follows to the letter the accountability mechanism provided under the law.

a3777.speaker: Moupo, Botswana opposition leader (response to the Budget Speech)
a3777.name: Moupo
a3777.title: Botswana opposition leader (response to the Budget Speech)
a3777.speech: Raised general issues that he said he had raised last year but that were not satisfactorily responded to, first among them the huge foreign exchange reserves kept in foreign banks: while substantial reserves are understandable both for financing the import of goods and services and for reasons of economic prudence, "it does not seem to make any economic sense to keep such excessive amounts of money idle in foreign banks," arguing that the huge challenges of development facing the country necessitate the use of at least part of those funds to finance development projects or for productive investment.

a4012.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, executive director of the Joint United Nations Program on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS)
a4012.name: Winnie Byanyima
a4012.title: executive director of the Joint United Nations Program on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS)
a4012.speech: Announced South African President Cyril Ramaphosa’s agreement to take charge of the upcoming three-year funding cycle of the Global Fund at a press conference in Johannesburg on Friday: “The Global Fund replenishment is critical and it’s great that South Africa has offered to lead that.”

a4012.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, executive director of the Joint United Nations Program on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS)
a4012.name: Winnie Byanyima
a4012.title: executive director of the Joint United Nations Program on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS)
a4012.speech: Told reporters that AIDS “is very much an African disease now, with 75% of people living with HIV being on this continent.”

a4012.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, executive director of the Joint United Nations Program on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS)
a4012.name: Winnie Byanyima
a4012.title: executive director of the Joint United Nations Program on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS)
a4012.speech: Said that a smaller amount of foreign aid means a plan to end the disease as a public health threat by 2030 “will get more and more off-track” ; said that while poor African countries are working hard to fill the sudden gap created by President Donald Trump’s decision to halt US aid, they are going to have to do more with less, and added that there was also an urgent need to restructure their debts to cut debt-service costs that can be many times larger than their healthcare budgets.

a4012.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, executive director of the Joint United Nations Program on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS)
a4012.name: Winnie Byanyima
a4012.title: executive director of the Joint United Nations Program on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS)
a4012.speech: “South Africa is a leader and the region itself has been making progress and can continue making progress in spite of the funding freeze by the American government”, but it “needs to move faster on reducing new infections”, and on ensuring key at-risk communities including migrants, men who have sex with men, sex workers and drug users have appropriate services.

a4100.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a4100.name: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a4100.speech: Announced on Monday, October 21, 2024, the suspension of its activities in the city of Djibo, in the north of Burkina Faso; the NGO said it took the decision following repeated incidents targeting health centers, water distribution points and its premises.

a4100.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a4100.name: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a4100.speech: Gave assurances that its teams will continue to provide humanitarian assistance in other regions of the country.

a4100.speaker: Dr. Moussa Ousman, MSF programme manager
a4100.name: Dr. Moussa Ousman
a4100.title: MSF programme manager
a4100.speech: “We need adequate security conditions to allow our teams to continue their mission and provide assistance to communities affected by insecurity and violence.” ; “We hope that the security situation will improve, giving us better guarantees for the protection of our teams and our activities, so that we can resume our assistance to Djibo.”

a4192.speaker: Sylvestre Amoussou, film director
a4192.name: Sylvestre Amoussou
a4192.title: film director
a4192.speech: On the messages of the film: “Through my film the main message concerns the fight against corruption. Corruption which exists both at the summit of the State and at the level of the ordinary citizen. ‘UN PAS EN AVANT – Les Dessous de la Corruption' cannot by itself change the African situation, but my main intention is to arouse in the viewer the desire to fight against corruption, to take part in local elections, thus taking a step towards democracy. In this film, I also give women back their place. Without women, man is nothing. And I think that with more women in the highest positions there would be less war. A woman always thinks of the future of her children and therefore of the future of her country.”

a4192.speaker: Sylvestre Amoussou, film director
a4192.name: Sylvestre Amoussou
a4192.title: film director
a4192.speech: On the Beninese anti-corruption law and screening the film in Benin: “I hope this will not be one more law that goes unapplied. I approached the government so that it would organise a screening in BENIN; for the moment that remains a dead letter. I deplore it because I think the government does not give a large enough place to cinema, which can develop a country both humanly and economically. Faced with globalisation, and in the internet era, the government has not grasped the full importance of owning and controlling its image both nationally and internationally. But I do not despair, quite the contrary.”

a4192.speaker: Sylvestre Amoussou, film director
a4192.name: Sylvestre Amoussou
a4192.title: film director
a4192.speech: On the film's originality and financing: “Its greatest originality: its mode of financing. Indeed, the majority of the funds come both from African civil society and from African politicians who are beginning to understand that only the image they finance can restore a positive image of the continent. Even if the film criticises current African society, it depicts a modern Africa, beautiful and winning. This image will never be financed by the West.” ; “I was supported by the government of Benin, Beninese civil society, the independent fund of France which contributed 70,000 euros, and the Moroccan cinema centre. The film is totally independent. I am free to say what I see fit. That is very important, because it is neither biased nor slanted. Most African films are financed by France. Which is problematic since in return she wants us to speak about her from her point of view. Moreover, the French media such as France Télévisions refuse to talk about this film because they do not want to give importance to a film that calls into question the relations France maintains with Africa. Few cinemas have agreed to show it. Only the director of the Espace Saint Michel in Paris agreed to show it because he based himself quite simply on the quality of the film. We hope the public will like it so that it will be shown in other cinemas.”

a4192.speaker: Sylvestre Amoussou, film director
a4192.name: Sylvestre Amoussou
a4192.title: film director
a4192.speech: On his financiers, some of whom may themselves be implicated in corruption: “In any case I hope so. But it is true that there is a whole education to be redone because the coloniser firmly anchored corruption in our civilisations and some Africans have totally appropriated it and have even become masters of it. Our dialects do not possess the word ‘corruption'. The French language does! And let us not forget that for there to be corrupted people there must at the base be corrupters.”

a4192.speaker: Sylvestre Amoussou, film director
a4192.name: Sylvestre Amoussou
a4192.title: film director
a4192.speech: On any confusion with the Beninese government: “No. The film was indeed entirely shot in Benin, it is simply a choice to showcase our country, through these beautiful landscapes and its infrastructural effort to meet international tourism standards. The country in which the film is set remains the United States of Africa. You can see moreover that its flag is a star-spangled banner representing all the African states. Nor is there any possible confusion between the current prime minister of BENIN and the corrupt prime minister of my film. For two main reasons: the first is that the post of prime minister did not exist in the government of BENIN at the time of shooting. The second reason is that my film, although shot in BENIN, does not speak of the case of BENIN but of a generic country situated in Africa. Let us not forget that the film also speaks of international corruption and of the abuse of NGOs. Beninese people know well that the current prime minister is the architect of the country's development. And supporting the screening of ‘UN PAS EN AVANT – Les Dessous de la Corruption' would only confirm the government's good will in its fight against corruption.”

a4192.speaker: Sylvestre Amoussou, film director
a4192.name: Sylvestre Amoussou
a4192.title: film director
a4192.speech: On his future projects: “I am currently working on another feature film which recounts the drama of North-South relations. Corruption must be fought for more democracy in Africa. But not in a brutal way as Westerners do. Let us denounce corruption in order to move forward and build a better world for our children. I think African cinema has a role to play. Making a film costs a great deal but Africa also needs to dream. If she wants to be independent she must finance her own image.”

a4364.speaker: Institutional Economists
a4364.name: Institutional Economists
a4364.speech: As institutional economists would say, the agriculture-dependent economy administered under the Emperor’s feudal structure was an “exploitative” system.

a4364.speaker: EPRDF (ruling front)
a4364.name: EPRDF (ruling front)
a4364.speech: Testified at the time that the system the country was following was “white capitalism”, and announced that it wanted to create a system in which supply and demand guide the market, basic economic inputs are under individual ownership, ownership of wealth is permitted without limit, market chains operate without quotas or pressure, market institutions organize freely, and wealth creation receives economic incentive.

a4364.speaker: Joseph Stiglitz, renowned economist and Nobel laureate (in his book “Globalization and Its Discontents”)
a4364.name: Joseph Stiglitz
a4364.title: renowned economist and Nobel laureate (in his book “Globalization and Its Discontents”)
a4364.speech: Describes how Ethiopia’s policymakers of the time (primarily Meles Zenawi) struggled hard to resist the policy pressure of the World Bank and the IMF and how, in the end, standing firm in refusal, they lost the temporary recovery financing they were to have received; Stiglitz calls this struggle a struggle to create independent policy-making capacity and says it rescued Ethiopia from the Structural Adjustment Program these institutions were spreading internationally at the time and from a process whose damage has still not disappeared in various economies.

a4364.speaker: Government of Ethiopia
a4364.name: Government of Ethiopia
a4364.speech: According to the government, the decision to privatise state development enterprises was made in order to create an inclusive, sustainable and modernised economy; the government itself also says the decision was a step taken to ease the debt burden, to obtain foreign exchange, to improve service delivery and to reduce government expenditure.

a4364.speaker: Ethiopian Reporter (editor’s note)
a4364.name: Ethiopian Reporter (editor’s note)
a4364.speech: From the editor: the writer is a finance-sector professional living in North America, and we note that the article reflects only his own views.

a4366.speaker: U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID)
a4366.name: U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID)
a4366.speech: According to USAID, in 2021 alone America provided approximately 8.5 billion dollars in aid to sub-Saharan Africa, funding healthcare, economic development, humanitarian assistance, and security programs ; according to USAID, Ethiopia received approximately 1.8 billion dollars in 2022 alone, making it one of the largest recipients of American aid in Africa.

a4366.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a4366.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a4366.speech: According to the WHO, more than 1.5 million African children receive life-saving vaccines annually through US-funded programmes.

a4366.speaker: Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis, & Malaria (GFATM)
a4366.name: Global Fund to Fight AIDS
a4366.title: Tuberculosis, & Malaria (GFATM)
a4366.speech: Reports that over 70pc of Africa’s HIV/AIDS programmes rely on international funding ; reports that over 60pc of Ethiopia’s HIV/AIDS programs rely on foreign aid.

a4366.speaker: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)
a4366.name: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)
a4366.speech: Estimates that 278 million people in Africa face chronic hunger.

a4366.speaker: Ethiopian Ministry of Health (MoH)
a4366.name: Ethiopian Ministry of Health (MoH)
a4366.speech: Estimates that the country needs at least 2 billion dollars annually to sustain essential health services.

a4366.speaker: 2001 Abuja Declaration
a4366.name: 2001 Abuja Declaration
a4366.speech: Recommended that at least 15pc of government spending go to healthcare, yet many countries fall short, relying on aid to fill the gap.

a4366.speaker: African Union
a4366.name: African Union
a4366.speech: According to the African Union, corruption costs Africa 148 billion dollars annually, money that could be used for healthcare, education, and infrastructure.

a4420.speaker: Benjamin Bol Mel, South Sudan Vice President for Economic Cluster
a4420.name: Benjamin Bol Mel
a4420.title: South Sudan Vice President for Economic Cluster
a4420.speech: Said civil servants and armed forces have received salary arrears for February and March 2025, in what he describes as the government's commitment to improving public service delivery ; In a statement on 24th March, said he has fulfilled his previous pledge to expedite the prompt payment of civil servant salaries on the 24th of every month ; further revealed that a roadmap for the progressive clearance of all outstanding salary arrears will be unveiled ; also said the Bank of South Sudan has now established what he referred to as “ring fenced” public salary account dedicated to salary disbursement.

a4420.speaker: Peter Lokuju Lotirmoi, Minister of Finance (Eastern Equatoria)
a4420.name: Peter Lokuju Lotirmoi
a4420.title: Minister of Finance (Eastern Equatoria)
a4420.speech: Speaking to a state-owned radio, confirmed the payments and urged public to be patient while waiting for the other accumulated arrears: “It is true that the vice president fulfilled whatever he promised. So, our people today, they are receiving their salaries. Everybody now is okay, because our vice president is serious in whatever he promised” ; “I want the people to be patient. Again, I want the people to be ready to receive the March salaries. Let them be patient for some five or four days. We are going to release the other ones also. They are already with us.”

a4420.speaker: Kokol Michael, SPLM-IO Member of Parliament
a4420.name: Kokol Michael
a4420.title: SPLM-IO Member of Parliament
a4420.speech: Appealed to Vice President Bol to promptly pay the pending months of civil servants’ salaries and called for economic reform to ensure the restoration of the value of South Sudan pounds: “I welcome and appreciate that one man given. We hope that the Vice President of Economic Cluster has to continue meeting what he has promised to the civil servant.” ; “What we are currently receiving is an arrears, not the salaries because the salaries are paid immediately at end of the month.” ; “The Vice President of Economic cluster has to strengthen the issue of economy so that specifically the rate of dollars and pounds can stabilize, dollars have become stronger and the pounds which civil servants are receiving is completely very low when we go to the market.”

a4420.speaker: Ajok Grace, a civil servant
a4420.name: Ajok Grace
a4420.title: a civil servant
a4420.speech: Expressed frustrations over delayed salary payment since 2024 which she said has made life difficult for citizens across the state: “Looking at the current situation of the citizens, we all know it has not been fine with us because people have been trying like struggling here and there” ; “Though the salary was not there, the sacrifice was being given to the services of the nation. But at the end of the day, you find all this duration of time, there are people who have been borrowing.” ; “There are some who tried investing in certain things and it was not working out. But since they had been promised something big, they were having that hope. So, looking at this one-month salary, I feel it’s not going to go well for citizens here.” ; “Though some of them might accept, generally, it’s not something good. at least if it was something that is more than three months, it would make some big deal. But just one month’s salary, that is something so bad.”

a4575.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4575.name: Donald Trump
a4575.title: US President
a4575.speech: Gave no guarantee of what the European leaders were expecting: he did not announce an immediate ceasefire; he reiterated that the agreement would be a three-way affair (Putin-Trump-Zelensky); that there would be territorial concessions of land that had belonged to Ukraine; and that there would be no American troops in Ukraine. Trump still finds in Putin a credible interlocutor for arriving at a lasting solution to this crisis.

a4610.speaker: Council of Ministers of Ethiopia (regulation)
a4610.name: Council of Ministers of Ethiopia (regulation)
a4610.speech: Has passed a regulation that would see fuel subsidies progressively lifted off in a year, with motorists carrying the full weight of global prices by July next year; the regulation introduces a six-month transition, with an estimated 300,000 public transport vehicles seeing a 10pc bi-annual rise in prices for five years and the remaining one million vehicle owners subjected to quarterly increases of 25pc for one year; it pledges stringent monitoring to prevent those receiving subsidised prices from selling fuel illegitimately, with administrative measures including revocation of subsidy privileges and criminal proceedings.

a4610.speaker: Federal authorities of Ethiopia
a4610.name: Federal authorities of Ethiopia
a4610.speech: Believe the gradual lifting of fuel subsidies is necessary to ease the “burden endured by low-income segments of the population.”

a4610.speaker: Ministry of Trade & Regional Integration officials
a4610.name: Ministry of Trade & Regional Integration officials
a4610.speech: Adjusted fuel prices last month by record-high increments under the pressure of rising import bills; its officials saw fit to cut subsidies by a quarter, leaving the cost to be shouldered by the public.

a4610.speaker: Ahmed Tusa, acting head of the Petroleum & Energy Authority
a4610.name: Ahmed Tusa
a4610.title: acting head of the Petroleum & Energy Authority
a4610.speech: Said during a media briefing last month that depreciation and rising costs in international markets have strained government coffers and that the increasing prices have tested the financial standing of the Ethiopian Petroleum Supply Enterprise.

a4610.speaker: An official following the case (anonymous)
a4610.name: An official following the case (anonymous)
a4610.speech: Disclosed that the deficit incurred by oil companies and fuel retailers due to the gradual lifting of subsidies will be refunded by the Enterprise with interest; said the refund period is not determined in the regulation, but it will be prompt so as not to hold up the companies' and dealers' working capital.

a4610.speaker: Ephrem Tesfaye, board member of the Petroleum Dealers' Association
a4610.name: Ephrem Tesfaye
a4610.title: board member of the Petroleum Dealers' Association
a4610.speech: Said that unless reimbursement is carried out on time, it will tie up cash for dealers who are already struggling to make cash-based payments for the fuel they receive ; on the risk of illicit trade under the dual-rate system: “I don't think the difference between the two prices is that attractive,” believing there is little to worry about ; “We'll see how efficient it will be.”

a4610.speaker: Teshager Amare, economist and consultant in commodity exchanges in African countries
a4610.name: Teshager Amare
a4610.title: economist and consultant in commodity exchanges in African countries
a4610.speech: Argues in favour of keeping the subsidies; worries any increase in the price of fuel comes with inflationary pressure; sees the decision to lift subsidies as ill-timed and advises officials to focus on developing a post-war recovery plan and rekindle economic activities before removing subsidies further. “Time should be taken to assess the impact of subsidies that have been lifted already.”

a4669.speaker: Duma Boko, President of Botswana
a4669.name: Duma Boko
a4669.title: President of Botswana
a4669.speech: Made the announcement of a public health state of emergency in a televised address on Monday, setting out a multi-million-pound plan to fix the health service supply chain under military supervision; said controlling the shortage would be “very sensitive on price because of our small treasury” ; “That work will continue without stopping until the entire procurement chain is put right”, announcing that the finance ministry had approved 250 million Botswana pula (£13.8m) in emergency funding ; stressed that the first consignment had begun shipping immediately from Gaborone, with rural areas of greatest need given priority ; “Current medicine prices have risen five to ten times above normal. In the current economic situation, this cannot be sustained.”

a4669.speaker: Ministry of Health of Botswana
a4669.name: Ministry of Health of Botswana
a4669.speech: Warned earlier this month that it was facing “major challenges,” including shortages of treatments and debts of more than one billion pula (Sh187 billion).

a4669.speaker: Dr Stephen Modise, Minister of Health of Botswana
a4669.name: Dr Stephen Modise
a4669.title: Minister of Health of Botswana
a4669.speech: Cited shortages including those of medicines and equipment for cancer control, HIV treatment and tuberculosis, among others.

a4669.speaker: UNAIDS
a4669.name: UNAIDS
a4669.speech: According to UNAIDS, before the cuts to American aid made by President Donald Trump, the United States financed one third of HIV funding in Botswana.

a4669.speaker: BBC (news agency)
a4669.name: BBC (news agency)
a4669.speech: Reported that Debswana, a joint venture between the government of Botswana and De Beers, saw its sales revenue fall by nearly 50 percent last year.

a4669.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a4669.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a4669.speech: According to the IMF, Botswana is the world's largest producer of diamonds by value, contributing a quarter of the country's GDP.

a4669.speaker: Debswana (quoted by local media)
a4669.name: Debswana (quoted by local media)
a4669.speech: Said this year's production would be cut to 15 million carats, a reduction of about 40 percent compared with the 2023 production level.

a4669.speaker: Bank of Tanzania (BoT) economic situation report, July 2025
a4669.name: Bank of Tanzania (BoT) economic situation report
a4669.title: July 2025
a4669.speech: Shows that in the year ending June 2025, gold brought in $3,804.5 million (Sh9.89 trillion), up from $3,121.8 million (Sh8.12 trillion) the previous year; the increase was attributed to good world market prices and purchases by the BoT; exports of goods and services rose to $16,926.4 million from $14,380.2 million in the same period of 2024.

a4669.speaker: Tanzania Basic Statistics Report 2024
a4669.name: Tanzania Basic Statistics Report 2024
a4669.speech: Shows that gold brought Sh8.851 trillion into the country in 2024, accounting for 69.07 percent of the Sh12.813 trillion obtained from all sales of natural products in 2024.

a4669.speaker: Dr Donath Olomi, economics and business expert
a4669.name: Dr Donath Olomi
a4669.title: economics and business expert
a4669.speech: Says what happened to Botswana is a lesson for Tanzania and other countries to ensure the economy and foreign trade do not depend on a single thing: “Now Botswana for many years had an economy that depended on diamonds; only recently did they begin to build other sectors such as cattle keeping and tourism, but these had not yet borne fruit to any great extent” ; said that for Tanzania such a situation is difficult because, although gold brings in a lot of money, there is also revenue from other products including agricultural and industrial goods ; “Our economy is spread out. It does not depend on one thing the way they depend so heavily on diamonds. Perhaps in the future, if gas is extracted and processed on a large scale and we get a lot of money from it, then our economy could be said to depend heavily on gas, which is dangerous, because if there are price changes or the market is affected, we are affected directly.”

a4669.speaker: Professor Aurelia Kamuzora, economics expert
a4669.name: Professor Aurelia Kamuzora
a4669.title: economics expert
a4669.speech: Recommends that greater effort be put into building various sectors, including agriculture, by adding value to the crops produced: “Let us not think that we can do it all by ourselves; let us invite people to come and help us add value to our crops and minerals so that we can broaden the scope for earning more money instead of depending on one thing” ; “These things will be possible by enabling people who have the intention of doing big things in this area; when someone starts something good that can bring in foreign exchange, financial institutions should look at how to enable him by giving him loans so that he can invest more in what he is doing” ; said business should not be left under the supervision of one person but linked with other sectors, and that enabling citizens to find capital should be looked at ; “In this we cannot refuse to continue inviting foreigners to continue to stand and work in areas we cannot manage, because if they leave it can affect the country; instead we can learn from them.”

a4669.speaker: Oscar Mkude, economics expert
a4669.name: Oscar Mkude
a4669.title: economics expert
a4669.speech: Says the problem is that nearly 80 percent of their needs they buy from abroad, depending on diamonds and tourism; said that when the countries that buy diamonds or send tourists have trouble, their country too loses revenue ; said the action by the United States of withdrawing aid and increasing tariffs on some things together affects their economy directly, because these are areas they depend on ; said a country can protect itself by having many sources for building the economy: “While other sources are affected, others will continue building the economy; during Covid-19, when tourism was faltering, activities such as agriculture continued as normal, a situation that enabled Tanzania to protect itself from a major economic decline compared with other areas.”

a4687.speaker: Dr. Nassirou Kassoumou, Director General of the Observatory of the Family, Women and Children (OFFE), Benin
a4687.name: Dr. Nassirou Kassoumou
a4687.title: Director General of the Observatory of the Family, Women and Children (OFFE), Benin
a4687.speech: Said that within the system of care, punishment and struggle against gender-based violence, the Observatory of the Family, Women and Children appears as a body of oversight — a strategic watchdog structure covering all the target groups of social action — designed and set up to document the various interventions carried out for vulnerable groups by protection services, whether the one-stop social protection desks, the former social promotion centres or other actors; “we are a structure that supports decision-making, a structure for monitoring and evaluating the impact of interventions, but a structure that provides the information and inputs needed to reorient actions in order to better achieve the objectives set.”

a4687.speaker: Dr. Nassirou Kassoumou, Director General of the Observatory of the Family, Women and Children (OFFE), Benin
a4687.name: Dr. Nassirou Kassoumou
a4687.title: Director General of the Observatory of the Family, Women and Children (OFFE), Benin
a4687.speech: Presented the OFFE as a scientific and social office created by the government of Benin whose essential mission is to produce evidence and information on the family and all its components in order to support better decision-making, with three key attributions: data collection, production and use of statistical data; the production of knowledge through action-research documenting social phenomena, both long-standing and emerging; and specialised communication on social action, making useful information available to journalists, researchers, academics, NGOs and partners.

a4687.speaker: Dr. Nassirou Kassoumou, Director General of the Observatory of the Family, Women and Children (OFFE), Benin
a4687.name: Dr. Nassirou Kassoumou
a4687.title: Director General of the Observatory of the Family, Women and Children (OFFE), Benin
a4687.speech: Said the OFFE has very good collaboration with all the structures involved in the fight against GBV in Benin — the sister structures of the Ministry of Social Affairs and Microfinance, the one-stop social protection desks (the former social promotion centres) which feed the data collection system, the ministry's technical directorate in charge of gender, the National Institute for Women outside the ministry, and civil society organisations, which are strategic partners whose statistical data are captured and aggregated into the national effort.

a4687.speaker: Dr. Nassirou Kassoumou, Director General of the Observatory of the Family, Women and Children (OFFE), Benin
a4687.name: Dr. Nassirou Kassoumou
a4687.title: Director General of the Observatory of the Family, Women and Children (OFFE), Benin
a4687.speech: Explained that SidoFFE-NG is the new-generation integrated data system on the family, women and children, the official public system for collecting and producing statistical data on social action in Benin, designed participatively and put into service in 2019; it produces each month around 400 routine indicator data points disaggregated by sex and age across four domains — child protection; promotion of the family, women and gender; social protection and national solidarity; and social inclusion of persons with disabilities and the elderly — through a dynamic web application hosted at Benin's national data centre, fed monthly by each commune's one-stop protection desk with data from police stations, republican police units, health facilities and civil society organisations, with quality controls before national consolidation; said it has become the reference system for reliable and current evidence, is accessible online at www.sidoffe-ng.social.gouv.bj, and enables the regular production of GBV information bulletins, the analytical report on gender-based violence and social dashboards.

a4687.speaker: Dr. Nassirou Kassoumou, Director General of the Observatory of the Family, Women and Children (OFFE), Benin
a4687.name: Dr. Nassirou Kassoumou
a4687.title: Director General of the Observatory of the Family, Women and Children (OFFE), Benin
a4687.speech: Said the OFFE was conceived to serve as a watchdog structure, a “conscientious objector”, and to provide a mechanism that acts as a mirror for social action, allowing actors to evaluate what they are doing — the trends, the sex-specific distribution of GBV, the groups and age brackets most affected in each commune and department — and that the OFFE, through SIDOFFE, is today the only structure that gives them all this reliable information.

a4687.speaker: Dr. Nassirou Kassoumou, Director General of the Observatory of the Family, Women and Children (OFFE), Benin
a4687.name: Dr. Nassirou Kassoumou
a4687.title: Director General of the Observatory of the Family, Women and Children (OFFE), Benin
a4687.speech: Cited the analytical report for 2023 (with the 2024 report currently being prepared), which shows that from 1 January to 31 December 2023, 30,372 cases of gender-based violence were recorded across all care structures in Benin, of which about 10,072 cases concerned children, i.e. persons under 18; said the OFFE has carried out more than twenty studies on the target groups of social action, including on sensitive themes such as witchcraft accusations involving children, and that the data show four leading forms of violence: psychological and moral violence, followed by economic violence, physical violence and sexual violence.

a4687.speaker: Dr. Nassirou Kassoumou, Director General of the Observatory of the Family, Women and Children (OFFE), Benin
a4687.name: Dr. Nassirou Kassoumou
a4687.title: Director General of the Observatory of the Family, Women and Children (OFFE), Benin
a4687.speech: Said SIDOFFE has become a think-tank reference in Africa and worldwide, which earned it election to the vice-presidency of the African Group on Gender Statistics — a group set up by UN Women and the African Development Bank — and that the OFFE is now a model for observatories in West Africa, with studies showing the Benin model is ahead of sub-Saharan African countries, many of which come to learn from the OFFE; added that fruitful partnerships begun last year with the African Centre for Equitable Development and organisations such as EngenderHealth show the OFFE has left an indelible imprint on the fight against gender-based violence.

a4748.speaker: Nthomeng Majara, Deputy Prime Minister of Lesotho (government gazette, “Declaration of National State of Disaster of Socio-Economic Effects on High Rate of Youth Unemployment and Job Losses in Lesotho”)
a4748.name: Nthomeng Majara
a4748.title: Deputy Prime Minister of Lesotho (government gazette, “Declaration of National State of Disaster of Socio-Economic Effects on High Rate of Youth Unemployment and Job Losses in Lesotho”)
a4748.speech: “Pursuant to Section 3 of the Disaster Management Act 1997 and acting on the advice of the Board through the Minister in the Prime Minister’s Office, I, Nthomeng Majara, Acting Prime Minister of Lesotho, declare a state of disaster of socio-economic effects on (the) high rate of youth unemployment and job losses in Lesotho. This declaration shall be for a period of two years, effective from the date of publication in the gazette to the 30th of June 2027.”

a4748.speaker: Sam Matekane, Prime Minister of Lesotho
a4748.name: Sam Matekane
a4748.title: Prime Minister of Lesotho
a4748.speech: At a press conference on 9 June 2025 announced a plan to create 62,000 jobs beginning 1 July 2025 ; during the National Youth Dialogue on 18 June 2025 acknowledged the severity of the unemployment crisis and encouraged the youth to continue engaging with the government and its partners in seeking solutions: “We believe in the saying that there is nothing for the youth without the youth.”

a4748.speaker: Opposition parties
a4748.name: Opposition parties
a4748.speech: Met the announcement with widespread skepticism, questioning the feasibility of creating so many jobs in such a short period.

a4748.speaker: Nthomeng Majara, Deputy Prime Minister of Lesotho
a4748.name: Nthomeng Majara
a4748.title: Deputy Prime Minister of Lesotho
a4748.speech: Speaking in an interview, explained that declaring a state of disaster allows the government to take extraordinary measures that are otherwise not possible under normal governance: “Declarations like these allow government to undertake interventions that it would not ordinarily be able to implement” ; “Most of the time, declarations like these give the government a chance to do activities that it would not be able to do under normal circumstances” ; added that the declaration provided an opportunity to invite development partners and allies to contribute to addressing the crisis: “It also helps to invite friends of the government such as development partners. Once you make a declaration, they start to realise that there is a serious problem, and they might want to help. Sometimes not with money, but with skills and opportunities” ; “While the primary focus of the declaration is on the youth, the plan is to address unemployment across the board. This includes those affected by reciprocal tariffs and the withdrawal of support by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID).”

a4748.speaker: Nthomeng Majara, Deputy Prime Minister of Lesotho
a4748.name: Nthomeng Majara
a4748.title: Deputy Prime Minister of Lesotho
a4748.speech: “Unemployment does not affect only the youth; it affects a lot of other people. The goal is to address unemployment in its entirety; it is just that the Prime Minister emphasised that the youth should not be left behind. Meaning the focus is on the youth, but we are going to address unemployment in its entirety. Sometimes you might find that many youths do not apply to a certain sector in the expected number. That doesn’t mean other people cannot apply or join that sector. So, to answer your question, this is not solely for the youth, but it focuses on the youth.”

a4748.speaker: Tšeliso Mokhosi, Lesotho’s Minister of Labour and Employment
a4748.name: Tšeliso Mokhosi
a4748.title: Lesotho’s Minister of Labour and Employment
a4748.speech: Speaking from Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, where he was attending the Africa Job Creation Summit, backed the declaration, saying it helps the government maintain focus on the problem: “We are in a crisis, and when we are in crisis, the gazette helps the government to focus on that problem. Take for example the issue of Covid-19: the state of disaster was declared, and money was channelled towards solving that problem at the time. Similarly, this state of disaster helps the government to release available funds into fighting the current youth unemployment.”

a4748.speaker: Tšeliso Mokhosi, Lesotho’s Minister of Labour and Employment
a4748.name: Tšeliso Mokhosi
a4748.title: Lesotho’s Minister of Labour and Employment
a4748.speech: Said young people had already expressed deep concerns about the skyrocketing unemployment rate, to the extent that they had even contemplated staging protests: “Remember the youth wrote to the Prime Minister, asking him to help with the situation of the high unemployment rate, and that it should be declared as a state of disaster. They even wrote to Parliament that they wanted to protest against unemployment. Every minister explained clearly how their ministries will tackle unemployment at Manthabiseng Convention Centre during the Youth Dialogue.”

a4975.speaker: The White House
a4975.name: The White House
a4975.speech: sees the three-day summit with the leaders of five African states as an "incredible" commercial opportunity.

a4975.speaker: Mohamed Ould Ghazouani, Mauritania President
a4975.name: Mohamed Ould Ghazouani
a4975.title: Mauritania President
a4975.speech: "In the short time you've been back in office, the last few months you came to the rescue for peace," ; "You rushed to Africa to resolve a longstanding problem," referring to a peace deal between DR Congo and Rwanda facilitated by the White House.

a4975.speaker: Other African state leaders at the lunch
a4975.name: Other African state leaders at the lunch
a4975.speech: echoed Ghazouani's remarks, most of them making direct comments in support of Trump being nominated for a Nobel Peace Prize.

a4975.speaker: Bassirou Diomaye Faye, Senegal President
a4975.name: Bassirou Diomaye Faye
a4975.title: Senegal President
a4975.speech: complimented Trump's golf skills, inviting him to build a golf course in Senegal.

a4975.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4975.name: Donald Trump
a4975.title: US President
a4975.speech: "Thank you very much. Very nice. Thank you. I didn't know I'd be treated this nicely. This is great," ; "We could do this all day long."

a4975.speaker: Bassirou Diomaye Faye, Senegal President
a4975.name: Bassirou Diomaye Faye
a4975.title: Senegal President
a4975.speech: spoke about the prospect of building a "tech city" in Dakar with "views of the sea", and said: "I would like to invite American investors to take part in this".

a4975.speaker: Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema, Gabon President
a4975.name: Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema
a4975.title: Gabon President
a4975.speech: said his country has "a great deal of resources", including rare earth minerals ; "You are welcome to come and invest, otherwise other countries might come instead of you."

a4975.speaker: Babacar Diagne, Senegal's former ambassador to Washington
a4975.name: Babacar Diagne
a4975.title: Senegal's former ambassador to Washington
a4975.speech: said the invitations to the African leaders reflected the recent "paradigm shift" in US policy towards the continent ; "It's not like before with the Democrats. There were two strong points with them: poverty reduction and development issues, through Agoa and other initiatives. All that is over" ; said the Trump administration's position will mirror how it has dealt with Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky: "Pure trade. It's give and take, win and win. We saw it with Ukraine. You sign the agreement on minerals and you'll have us on your side, otherwise, you forget everything."

a4975.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4975.name: Donald Trump
a4975.title: US President
a4975.speech: cut US aid to the continent, saying it was wasteful and incompatible with his "America First" policy.

a4975.speaker: Nicaise Mouloumbi, head of a leading non-governmental organisation in Gabon
a4975.name: Nicaise Mouloumbi
a4975.title: head of a leading non-governmental organisation in Gabon
a4975.speech: said the Trump administration's focus on Africa was down to increasing competition from rival powers - including China and Russia - for its prized resources: "All these [invited] countries have important minerals: gold, oil, manganese, gas, wood and zircon - Senegal, Mauritania and Gabon, in particular" ; added that the US might be most keen to strengthen ties with Gabon not only because it had "strategic" minerals like manganese and uranium, as well as oil, but also because it was strategically located along the Gulf of Guinea, with a coastline of about 800km, and could host a US military base that America plans to build in the region.

a4975.speaker: Babacar Diagne, Senegal's former ambassador to Washington
a4975.name: Babacar Diagne
a4975.title: Senegal's former ambassador to Washington
a4975.speech: made a similar point about piracy, saying that "maritime terrorism in the Gulf of Guinea has become an extremely important issue" for the US.

a4975.speaker: Ousmane Sene, head of the West African Research Centre (WARC)
a4975.name: Ousmane Sene
a4975.title: head of the West African Research Centre (WARC)
a4975.speech: said migration will be central to discussions for Mauritania and Senegal: "Let's not forget that between 2023 and 2025, no fewer than 20,000 young Mauritanians left for the US via Nicaragua, along with hundreds of young Senegalese" ; "All these countries are also departure points for illegal emigration" ; "That's an extremely important point in his [Trump's] migration policy, and every day people are turned back at the borders."

a4975.speaker: Sources (anonymous, cited by Semafor)
a4975.name: Sources (anonymous
a4975.title: cited by Semafor)
a4975.speech: have told Semafor that restoring Mauritania's diplomatic ties with Israel may be a sticking point for any would-be White House deal.

a4975.speaker: Umaro Cissoko Embalo, President of Guinea-Bissau
a4975.name: Umaro Cissoko Embalo
a4975.title: President of Guinea-Bissau
a4975.speech: "Guinea-Bissau has now emerged from a state of disorder to become a real state. The Americans do not invite just any state to their country - only a well-structured state," he was quoted as saying at the airport before he left for Washington.

a5022.speaker: Brigadier General Shawn Holtz, Deputy Director of Strategy, Engagement and Programs, US Africa Command (Africom)
a5022.name: Brigadier General Shawn Holtz
a5022.title: Deputy Director of Strategy, Engagement and Programs, US Africa Command (Africom)
a5022.speech: Recalled that strong relationships reduce the overall cost of security while preventing malicious actors and rogue states from exploiting vulnerable populations ; stressed the importance of fostering collaboration, resilience and the creation of a sustainable security framework in the face of emerging challenges.

a5022.speaker: Brian Shukan, US Ambassador to Benin
a5022.name: Brian Shukan
a5022.title: US Ambassador to Benin
a5022.speech: Welcomed the meeting, describing it as a major turning point in bilateral relations: “Our partnership has continued to grow thanks to our shared determination to strengthen the security of our peoples, and to contribute to that of the African continent” ; “Together, we draw on our unique strengths and perspectives to confront complex challenges” ; specified that the alliance between the United States and Benin is strategic, aiming to promote security, encourage stability and foster the prosperity of the two nations.

a5022.speaker: Major General Abou Issa, Chief of Staff of the Beninese Army (speaking on behalf of the Minister of Defence)
a5022.name: Major General Abou Issa
a5022.title: Chief of Staff of the Beninese Army (speaking on behalf of the Minister of Defence)
a5022.speech: Recalled the historic importance of this cooperation and expressed his confidence in its future, stressing that the meeting embodies the solidity of the ties between the two countries ; “The fight against terrorism requires cross-border and transnational coordination” ; noted the complexity of the challenges facing the two nations and that the response must be flexible and adapted to changing contexts, while showing pragmatism, creativity and cooperation.

a5033.speaker: Xi Jinping, Chinese President
a5033.name: Xi Jinping
a5033.title: Chinese President
a5033.speech: Put forward the principles of China’s Africa policy – sincerity, real results, amity and good faith, and pursuing the greater good and shared interests, charting the course for China’s cooperation with Africa, and providing the fundamental guidelines.

a5033.speaker: President Xi Jinping and African leaders, at the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC) Beijing Summit
a5033.name: President Xi Jinping and African leaders
a5033.title: at the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC) Beijing Summit
a5033.speech: Unanimously decided that the two sides would work to build an even stronger China-Africa community of shared future, advance cooperation under the Belt and Road Initiative, establishing a new milestone in China-Africa relations.

a5033.speaker: China (government)
a5033.name: China (government)
a5033.speech: Has announced an exemption from debt incurred in the form of interest-free Chinese government loans due to mature by the end of 2018, applying to Africa’s least developed countries, heavily indebted and poor countries, landlocked developing countries and small island developing countries that have diplomatic relations with China.

a5033.speaker: China (at the China-Africa Internet Development and Cooperation Forum, August 2021)
a5033.name: China (at the China-Africa Internet Development and Cooperation Forum
a5033.title: August 2021)
a5033.speech: Announced its intention to formulate and implement a joint China-Africa Partnership Plan on Digital Innovation in Africa.

a5033.speaker: FOCAC Beijing Summit 2018 (China and Africa)
a5033.name: FOCAC Beijing Summit 2018 (China and Africa)
a5033.speech: Reached a strategic agreement to build a China-Africa community of shared future characterized by joint responsibility, win-win cooperation, happiness for all, cultural prosperity, common security, and harmony between humanity and nature.

a5262.speaker: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.name: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.speech: Urged the International Court of Justice to expedite its decision on the merits of the lawsuit filed by the Republic of South Africa against Israel on charges of its failure to fulfil its obligations under the 1948 Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of Genocide, based on the Court's finding that the Palestinian people are protected under the Convention and on Israel's failure, as the occupying power, to comply with the provisional measures ordered by the Court on 26/1/2024, 28/3/2024 and 24/5/2024.

a5262.speaker: Resolution of the 162nd session of the Council of the Arab League at the level of Arab foreign ministers
a5262.name: Resolution of the 162nd session of the Council of the Arab League at the level of Arab foreign ministers
a5262.speech: Affirmed that there is consensus among the member states of the League of Arab States and the parties to the 1948 Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of Genocide to formally intervene in support of the lawsuit brought by South Africa against Israel before the International Court of Justice regarding its violation of its obligations under the Convention during the brutal and ongoing Israeli aggression on the Gaza Strip.

a5262.speaker: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.name: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.speech: Affirmed its support for President Mahmoud Abbas's decision to travel to the Gaza Strip with the aim of halting the ongoing aggression against the Strip and securing the complete and immediate withdrawal of the Israeli occupation forces, affirming that the State of Palestine has jurisdiction over the entire territory of the state, restoring national unity under the umbrella of the Palestine Liberation Organisation, and enabling the government to carry out its duties effectively throughout the Palestinian territory.

a5262.speaker: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.name: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.speech: Urged the International Criminal Court to move forward in taking the measures it has called for, by issuing arrest warrants against the leaders of the Israeli occupation, especially in light of the conclusion of the Office of the Prosecutor of the Court that there are reasonable grounds to believe that they have committed crimes falling under the Court's jurisdiction.

a5262.speaker: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.name: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.speech: Affirmed its categorical rejection of the plans of Israel, the occupying power, for the day after the Israeli aggression, and rejected its control over any part of the Gaza Strip ; The ministers demanded Israel's complete withdrawal from the Gaza Strip, including the Salah al-Din "Philadelphia" axis and the Palestinian side of the Rafah crossing, considering that the Palestinian-Egyptian border is a sovereign border that cannot be violated, and the necessity of operating the Rafah crossing in accordance with the applicable rules and removing all obstacles to safe, appropriate and rapid humanitarian access through the crossing.

a5262.speaker: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.name: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.speech: Urged the member states to provide the necessary financial support to the State of Palestine and to activate a transparent and agreed Arab financial safety net to confront the economic and financial punitive measures that Israel practises against the State of Palestine, including the withholding and piracy of tax funds to which it is entitled ; Stressed the importance of the Arab countries continuing to support the budget of the State of Palestine and meeting their due and future obligations as quickly as possible in accordance with the resolutions of the Arab summits, and thanked the Republic of Algeria, which recently paid 105.6 million dollars, and the Republic of Iraq, which paid 20 million dollars, as contributions to supporting the budget of the State of Palestine.

a5262.speaker: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.name: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.speech: Called on the General Secretariat, in coordination with the member states, to implement the Arab summit resolution (No. 854 D.C. 33) adopted in the Kingdom of Bahrain, to include extremist Israeli organisations and groups that storm the blessed Al-Aqsa Mosque and are linked to Israeli colonial settlement on Arab national terrorist lists, to announce the list of shame of Israeli persons who broadcast genocidal rhetoric and incitement against the Palestinian people in preparation for legal measures against them, and to take the necessary measures to boycott all companies operating in illegal Israeli colonies in the occupied Palestinian and Arab territories.

a5262.speaker: Arab foreign ministers
a5262.name: Arab foreign ministers
a5262.speech: Called for the necessity of adopting and supporting Palestine's approach to obtaining full membership in the United Nations, and called on the Security Council to accept this membership on the basis of UN General Assembly resolution No. A/ES-10/L.30 of 9/5/2024, and to adopt and support the right of the State of Palestine to join international organisations and conventions with the aim of strengthening its legal and international status and embodying its independence and sovereignty over its territory.

a5262.speaker: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.name: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.speech: Instructed the Arab group in New York to begin steps to freeze Israel's participation in the UN General Assembly because of its failure to comply with the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, its threat to international peace and security, and its failure to fulfil the obligations that were a condition of its membership, and on the basis of the advisory opinion issued by the International Court of Justice, by submitting a request to the President of the General Assembly and through him to the Credentials Committee, and mobilising the necessary international support for it.

a5262.speaker: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.name: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.speech: Expressed its rejection of the claims and lies repeated by the Prime Minister of the occupation government in a desperate attempt to justify his refusal to withdraw from the Salah al-Din "Philadelphia" axis, and considered them claims aimed at obstructing the ceasefire efforts and the exchange of prisoners and hostages carried out by Egypt, Qatar and the United States, and that these claims constitute attempts to divert attention from the violations and the aggressive and inflammatory policy Israel has pursued against the Palestinian people throughout the occupied Palestinian territory.

a5262.speaker: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.name: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.speech: Condemned the crime of genocide against the Palestinian people in the Gaza Strip over a period of more than 11 months, and strongly condemned the systematic and widespread Israeli crimes and policies against the Palestinian people in the occupied West Bank aimed at displacing them from their land, the systematic destruction of Palestinian towns, villages, camps and infrastructure, the terrorism of Israeli colonists, the killing and wounding of hundreds of Palestinian citizens, the demolition, burning and destruction of houses, farms and property, and the arrest of thousands of Palestinians under inhumane conditions.

a5262.speaker: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.name: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.speech: Called on the international community to activate the advisory opinion delivered by the International Court of Justice, which affirmed the illegality of Israel's continued presence in the occupied Palestinian territory and that Israel is obliged to end its unlawful presence as quickly as possible, immediately cease and dismantle all colonial activities, evacuate the colonists from Palestinian land, and pay compensation for the damage caused ; Stressed that all states and international organisations are obliged not to recognise the legitimacy of the situation resulting from the unlawful presence of the Israeli occupation and not to provide aid or assistance in maintaining it, and that the United Nations, especially the General Assembly and the Security Council, must consider specific modalities and further measures to end that presence, and called on the General Secretariat to prepare a plan with member states to activate the advisory opinion.

a5262.speaker: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.name: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.speech: Appreciated the efforts of the non-permanent Arab member of the Security Council, the People's Democratic Republic of Algeria, in following up on developments in the Palestinian question in the Security Council, halting the Israeli aggression on the Gaza Strip and reaching a ceasefire, and supporting Palestine's request for full membership of the United Nations.

a5262.speaker: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.name: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.speech: Warned of the dangerous terrorist acts and movements led by some members of the far-right Israeli government in the occupied city of Jerusalem, including the escalating incursions into the blessed Al-Aqsa Mosque by thousands of Israeli colonists and the recently announced plans to build a Jewish synagogue in the mosque, warning that these dangerous and provocative acts of terrorism will lead to the ignition of a religious war in the region ; Strongly condemned the aggressive Israeli measures directed against the Islamic and Christian shrines in the city of Jerusalem, especially the blessed Al-Aqsa Mosque, including undermining freedom of worship, preventing worshippers from entering, storming and defiling it, vandalising its contents, holding Talmudic rituals in it, and attempts to change its existing historical and legal situation and divide it temporally and spatially.

a5262.speaker: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.name: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.speech: Affirmed its support for the efforts undertaken by the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan to protect the Islamic and Christian holy sites in the occupied city of Jerusalem, stressed the role of the Hashemite custodianship, and stressed that the Jordanian Department of Jerusalem Endowments and Al-Aqsa Mosque Affairs is the exclusive legal authority with jurisdiction to manage the affairs of the blessed Al-Aqsa Mosque, as well as the role of the Al-Quds Committee and the Bayt Mal Al-Quds Al-Sharif Agency.

a5262.speaker: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.name: Council of the Arab League (at the level of foreign ministers)
a5262.speech: Expressed its rejection and condemnation of the aggressive policies and measures taken by the Israeli occupation government against the embodiment of the independence of the State of Palestine, the intensification of plans to annex the territories of the occupied West Bank, colonial expansion of settlements, and the confiscation of thousands of dunams of Palestinian land, and condemned Israel's intensification of the policy of annexation and settlement in the occupied Syrian Golan ; Stressed that Israel's commission of the crime of displacing the Palestinian people outside their land is a grave violation of international humanitarian law, amounts to a declaration of war and an attack on Arab national security, and leads to the collapse of the chances for peace and aggravates the conflict in the region.

a5370.speaker: Malawi Energy Regulatory Authority (MERA) (statement)
a5370.name: Malawi Energy Regulatory Authority (MERA) (statement)
a5370.speech: Has announced an immediate ban on the purchase of petrol in jerrycans or drums from any fuel service station across the country, effective immediately, to support fuel importers in restoring the security of fuel supply as quickly as possible ; warned that any fuel service station found selling petrol in jerrycans will face immediate suspension of its operating license ; urged the public to report any instances of illegal fuel trading practices to MERA.

a5406.speaker: Patrick Achi, Minister of State and special adviser to President Alassane Ouattara (former Prime Minister of Cote d'Ivoire)
a5406.name: Patrick Achi
a5406.title: Minister of State and special adviser to President Alassane Ouattara (former Prime Minister of Cote d'Ivoire)
a5406.speech: Presented Cote d'Ivoire's economic assets, emphasising the local processing of agricultural products as well as the opportunities offered in infrastructure, energy, transport, agriculture, mining, industry and digital technology; encouraged American companies to become more involved in these strategic sectors.

a5406.speaker: Patrick Achi, Minister of State and special adviser to President Alassane Ouattara (former Prime Minister of Cote d'Ivoire)
a5406.name: Patrick Achi
a5406.title: Minister of State and special adviser to President Alassane Ouattara (former Prime Minister of Cote d'Ivoire)
a5406.speech: On behalf of the Head of State, expressed Cote d'Ivoire's gratitude for the support of the American government, notably through the $360 million MCC financing to strengthen the country's energy potential and its role as a regional hub; also welcomed the support of the US Exim Bank in financing the Cybastion projects intended to modernise Ivorian digital infrastructure.

a5406.speaker: Dr Massad Boulos, senior adviser for Africa to US President Donald Trump
a5406.name: Dr Massad Boulos
a5406.title: senior adviser for Africa to US President Donald Trump
a5406.speech: Presented the strategic orientations of the Trump administration, which now favours private investment and the growth of trade over traditional public aid - an approach described as "win-win", aimed at stimulating both the American and Ivorian economies ; gave his agreement in principle to make an official visit to Cote d'Ivoire in the coming weeks in order to deepen the discussions.

a5699.speaker: Le Globe France (French publication, article)
a5699.name: Le Globe France (French publication
a5699.title: article)
a5699.speech: published an article on the disunity and weakness of the Central African opposition on the eve of the presidential elections in the Central African Republic; noted that instead of focusing on developing a strategy to win the elections, the Central African opposition is mired in internal conflicts.

a5699.speaker: Crépin Mboli-Goumba, leader of PATRIE
a5699.name: Crépin Mboli-Goumba
a5699.title: leader of PATRIE
a5699.speech: accused the URCA of running disinformation campaigns.

a5699.speaker: Crépin Mboli-Goumba, leader of PATRIE
a5699.name: Crépin Mboli-Goumba
a5699.title: leader of PATRIE
a5699.speech: declared during the “Patara” debate with the Central African government representative Maxime Balalou on Ndéké Luka radio that it was necessary to establish a dialogue with President Touadéra.

a5699.speaker: Bertin Béa, member of the Kwa Na Kwa movement
a5699.name: Bertin Béa
a5699.title: member of the Kwa Na Kwa movement
a5699.speech: also announced his arrival in Bangui.

a5699.speaker: Central African press
a5699.name: Central African press
a5699.speech: reports more and more often that Martin Ziguélé is losing the respect and favour of former party members.

a5699.speaker: Cameroonian and Senegalese media
a5699.name: Cameroonian and Senegalese media
a5699.speech: According to them, Mr. Macron assured Mr. Meckassoua of his support in the coming presidential elections and urged him to sabotage them.

a5814.speaker: Somaliland National Electoral Commission (NEC)
a5814.name: Somaliland National Electoral Commission (NEC)
a5814.speech: said on Tuesday that Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi – also known as Irro – of the Waddani Party received close to 64 percent of the vote, beating the incumbent, President Muse Bihi Abdi of the Kulmiye Party, according to local media and The Associated Press news agency.

a5814.speaker: Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi (Irro) and Muse Bihi Abdi, presidential candidates
a5814.name: Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi (Irro) and Muse Bihi Abdi
a5814.title: presidential candidates
a5814.speech: Both candidates had campaigned promising they would resuscitate an ailing economy and push efforts to gain international recognition for Somaliland.

a5814.speaker: Several leading US Department of State officials who worked on Africa policy during Donald Trump's first term
a5814.name: Several leading US Department of State officials who worked on Africa policy during Donald Trump's first term
a5814.speech: have publicly voiced support for recognising Somaliland.

a5914.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Mali (statement issued by transitional president Assimi Goïta)
a5914.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Mali (statement issued by transitional president Assimi Goïta)
a5914.speech: Announced that Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso, members of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES), have introduced a common 0.5% customs duty on imports from other countries: “Goods imported from third countries and released for consumption or free circulation within the customs territory of the AES shall be subject to the confederation levy in accordance with its current customs regulations”; it is noted that the rate “may be revised by decision of the college of heads of state of the AES confederation,” with the collected funds to be allocated for financing its projects and programmes.

a5937.speaker: Advocate Salemane Phafane, Lesotho Football Association (LeFA) president
a5937.name: Advocate Salemane Phafane
a5937.title: Lesotho Football Association (LeFA) president
a5937.speech: Said he was humbled by the election judging by the number of 186 votes in favour as against the two who voted against him and his colleagues in the committee, and said this was a huge indictment on them to deliver on the mandate given to them by the international football community: “When I was elected into the FIFA Disciplinary Committee four years back, I thought that was the climax. So, I did not even dream or anticipate that one day I will serve in a more prestigious, elaborate and busier committee.” ; “Whenever you are elected to a higher position you become a better person…When elected into previous committees I served, I thought I knew it all, but I continued learning until the world realised that I have learnt enough and I can lead in world football.”

a5937.speaker: Advocate Salemane Phafane, LeFA president
a5937.name: Advocate Salemane Phafane
a5937.title: LeFA president
a5937.speech: Told the Lesotho Times that the skills he had acquired over time had helped transform the LeFA “into an organized, dynamic, and compliant organization”: “While we may stumble at times, we are generally among the most compliant organizations, not only in COSAFA and Africa, but in the world. We are not boasting, but we prioritize good governance in everything we do.”

a5937.speaker: Advocate Salemane Phafane, LeFA president
a5937.name: Advocate Salemane Phafane
a5937.title: LeFA president
a5937.speech: Said the LeFA faces major challenges including a comatose economy, limited player pool, lack of infrastructure, and insufficient government support ; “FIFA has a policy of funding infrastructure projects in countries where the senior national teams play their home games in their home territories and not in foreign soil as it is the case now. In Lesotho's case, where the national teams have to play home games on foreign soil due to the unavailability of CAF-approved grounds, FIFA has halted the infrastructure funding.” ; stressed that this was a major setback, as quality infrastructure is crucial for improving Lesotho's football.

a5937.speaker: Advocate Salemane Phafane, LeFA president
a5937.name: Advocate Salemane Phafane
a5937.title: LeFA president
a5937.speech: Appealed to the government to fulfill its responsibilities and support the development of football and sports in the country: “The government should have empathy for Basotho children who play football. For many years, the government of Lesotho has neglected its duty to fund football and sports in general.”

a5937.speaker: Advocate Salemane Phafane, LeFA president
a5937.name: Advocate Salemane Phafane
a5937.title: LeFA president
a5937.speech: Said the decision not to enrol league champions in international competitions has negatively impacted the growth of football in the country: “Having no team going for CAF Champions League has decreased competitiveness of football and it also denies our players international exposure.”

a5937.speaker: Advocate Salemane Phafane, LeFA president
a5937.name: Advocate Salemane Phafane
a5937.title: LeFA president
a5937.speech: Expressed frustration that politicians in Lesotho often misuse football for political gain, organizing tournaments as campaign strategies before elections, but then neglect the sport once in office: “This is unfortunate behaviour by our politicians. They misuse or abuse football.
