Whenever elections are approaching, they start organising soccer tournaments using them as one of their campaigning strategies, but once they are in government they forget about the sport…We are finding a solution to that, it will soon come to an end.”

a5937.speaker: Advocate Salemane Phafane, LeFA president
a5937.name: Advocate Salemane Phafane
a5937.title: LeFA president
a5937.speech: Acknowledged that Lesotho's small population and struggling economy “make it challenging to thrive in football”: “With the current status of our economy it is difficult to secure sponsors, and we have to solely depend on FIFA and CAF funding. But there are some companies who are trying their best as they continue to sponsor our league and tournaments, and we hope slowly we will get there.” ; “The other disadvantage is the limited population we must select players from as compared to other countries with big populations. To combat that challenge we have started searching and calling foreign based players who have roots in Lesotho to come and join our national teams.”

a5937.speaker: Advocate Salemane Phafane, LeFA president
a5937.name: Advocate Salemane Phafane
a5937.title: LeFA president
a5937.speech: “The academy is a huge achievement, and we are looking forward to having more. We are the second after Malawi to have this kind of project in the region and the first to do it before arrival of FIFA funding.” ; highlighted other achievements during the current strategic plan period, including assistant referee Souru Phatšoane's inclusion to officiate at the Olympic and World Cup games ; “We are moving at the right pace to achieve the targets we have set, but we can do better.”

a5937.speaker: Advocate Salemane Phafane, LeFA president
a5937.name: Advocate Salemane Phafane
a5937.title: LeFA president
a5937.speech: Acknowledged that while the country is excelling in other areas, its national teams have struggled to achieve success on the international stage: “In almost every department we can safely say we are doing well, but where we are not doing well is in the field of play,” adding the association was doing its best to address this challenge ; noted that Lesotho has been consistently exporting talent to foreign leagues in recent seasons, which he sees as a positive development, while expressing concern over the lack of a robust and successful football ecosystem in the country.

a5937.speaker: Advocate Salemane Phafane, LeFA president
a5937.name: Advocate Salemane Phafane
a5937.title: LeFA president
a5937.speech: Said the association trains coaches to meet the market demand for qualified and licensed professionals but complained these coaches were not being put to efficient use by clubs ; revealed that certain clubs prefer to borrow coaching licenses from top coaches just to meet registration and licensing requirements, describing the practice as “fraud” and explaining that “teams will list a CAF A-licensed coach as their official head coach for compliance purposes, but the day-to-day coaching responsibilities are handled by less qualified staff” ; “This happens in a way that a team borrows a licence from a particular CAF A-licensed coach to appear as their coach in the registration system, but only to find out that is only for compliance, the actual work continues to be done by a lower-licensed coach.”

a5937.speaker: Advocate Salemane Phafane, LeFA president
a5937.name: Advocate Salemane Phafane
a5937.title: LeFA president
a5937.speech: Addressed the absence of the Under-23 national team, which he said could have served as a feeder to the senior team, attributing this to lack of support from the government and the Lesotho National Olympic Committee (LNOC): “Under-23 team is mainly assembled for Olympic Games, and that says having an Under-23 will require massive support from LNOC, but I do not remember them fulfilling such responsibility even at once. So, it will be difficult for us to maintain such a team on our own.”

a5997.speaker: Amin Modad, Liberia's Commerce Minister
a5997.name: Amin Modad
a5997.title: Liberia's Commerce Minister
a5997.speech: Says the Ministry has improved revenue significantly and is poised to surpass $2.5m as it has commenced an aggressive assessment of rural services and a robust business registration exercise ; "Last year, the MOCI (Ministry of Commerce and Industry) projected $3M in revenue, but achieved only $1.9." ; "To date, we have generated about $1.9M and are poised to surpass $2.5 as we have commenced an aggressive assessment of our rural services and a robust business registration exercise."

a5997.speaker: Amin Modad, Liberia's Commerce Minister
a5997.name: Amin Modad
a5997.title: Liberia's Commerce Minister
a5997.speech: Reassured the public that the Ministry works diligently and focuses on establishing a predictable, vibrant, and enabling business environment ; "I remain committed fully to empowering Liberian businesses. Coming from the private sector, I KNOW what it means, and I understand the challenges Liberian entrepreneurs face."

a5997.speaker: Amin Modad, Liberia's Commerce Minister
a5997.name: Amin Modad
a5997.title: Liberia's Commerce Minister
a5997.speech: Noted that the MOCI has begun engaging stakeholders on the 25% Procurement Law, which mandates that 25% of public procurement must go to Liberian Businesses, with 5% specifically for women-owned MSMEs; disclosed that, in collaboration with the Public Procurement and Concession Commission (PPCC), the Ministry has reprioritized this and will solicit reports from each government agency to ensure compliance.

a5997.speaker: Amin Modad, Liberia's Commerce Minister
a5997.name: Amin Modad
a5997.title: Liberia's Commerce Minister
a5997.speech: Said his leadership grounded the Inspectorate for a while, the intent being to reorient the Inspectorate on its functions and responsibilities and address the numerous public complaints ; "We have relaunched the inspectorate with proper uniforms and a predictable inspection mandate. We have purchased a new pickup truck and appropriated other vehicles to improve its outreach." ; "We have curtailed cross border outward smuggling of rice, flour, and other commodities as well as inward smuggling of unhealthy foods, pharmaceuticals, and other commodities." ; reported that the MOCI has surpassed prior revenue collection on fines due to the vigilance of the Inspectorate in identifying malpractices.

a5997.speaker: Amin Modad, Liberia's Commerce Minister
a5997.name: Amin Modad
a5997.title: Liberia's Commerce Minister
a5997.speech: Disclosed that the Ministry has completed a Made in Liberia Store at the ministry to properly showcase and market Made in Liberia products supporting Liberian manufacturers and Agro processors, and said they will be visiting the Roberts International Airport (RIA) this week to replicate this, targeting travelers ; "These are proud establishments to provide market access and showcase Liberian products and culture."

a5997.speaker: Amin Modad, Liberia's Commerce Minister
a5997.name: Amin Modad
a5997.title: Liberia's Commerce Minister
a5997.speech: Detailed that the Ministry has secured funding to renovate the Farmers Market at the Jorkpentown Market to revive it for selling Liberian agricultural produce, said the top floor of the market was managed by the MOCI but was neglected over the years, the roofing system totally damaged and rain now pouring down to the market hall ; "We also contributed $2000 to LMA (Liberia Marketing Association) to support the renovation of the Rally-Time Market Roof which was causing a lot of distress for the marketers."

a5997.speaker: Amin Modad, Liberia's Commerce Minister
a5997.name: Amin Modad
a5997.title: Liberia's Commerce Minister
a5997.speech: Said the Ministry collected random samples of products such as zinc, steel, electric wires, and nails and sent them to its Standard Facility and the Ghana Standards Authority for testing, and stated that the Ministry recently released new Administrative Regulations on the importation of Electronics, Rice, and Frozen Foods aimed at opening the market in a more efficient (managed) manner with a focus on ensuring quality, fair pricing, increased government revenue, and empowering Liberians.

a5997.speaker: Amin Modad, Liberia's Commerce Minister
a5997.name: Amin Modad
a5997.title: Liberia's Commerce Minister
a5997.speech: Said the Ministry announced the reduction of the prices of key commodities and items beginning with Flour, Steel Rods, and Eggs ; "We have had several meetings with Importers and Supermarkets over the last two months and this list will be expanded shortly to cooking oils and other essentials."

a5997.speaker: Amin Modad, Liberia's Commerce Minister
a5997.name: Amin Modad
a5997.title: Liberia's Commerce Minister
a5997.speech: Said the Ministry has managed the rice trade strategically - Liberia has not experienced any shortage of rice and prices have remained stable - and announced that on September 27, India reduced its 20% tariff on rice by 10%, which will have a positive impact on stabilizing the price of rice on the market ; "With the leadership of the President, the strategy we employed over the last 9 months worked." ; "We have gone beyond rice. Our strategy and focus are more on food security. In collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture and the NIC, we are focusing on the diversification of local food production."

a6027.speaker: Mauro Vieira, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Brazil
a6027.name: Mauro Vieira
a6027.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs of Brazil
a6027.speech: Stressed that the members of this group of emerging economies agreed that "it is not in our interest to live in a fractured world" and that it is necessary to "strengthen multilateralism."

a6027.speaker: Mauro Vieira, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Brazil
a6027.name: Mauro Vieira
a6027.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs of Brazil
a6027.speech: Without once referring to US President Donald Trump, stressed that the group has the "willingness to promote a proactive agenda," in favour of the Paris Agreement, and that the "BRICS can lead" on issues such as climate change and Artificial Intelligence ; justified the absence of a final declaration by explaining that a joint final declaration will be issued during the meeting of heads of state, scheduled for 6 and 7 July in Rio de Janeiro.

a6027.speaker: BRICS foreign ministers (11 ministers meeting in Rio de Janeiro)
a6027.name: BRICS foreign ministers (11 ministers meeting in Rio de Janeiro)
a6027.speech: Reinforced "the firm refusal by all of them of the resurgence of trade protectionism."

a6027.speaker: Brazilian presidency communiqué (BRICS chair statement)
a6027.name: Brazilian presidency communiqué (BRICS chair statement)
a6027.speech: On the war and Russia's invasion of Ukraine, stated only that the "ministers recalled their national positions regarding the conflict in Ukraine, as expressed in the appropriate forums, including the Security Council and the United Nations General Assembly" ; "They noted with appreciation relevant mediation and good-offices proposals, including the African Peace Initiative and the creation of the Group of Friends for Peace, aimed at a peaceful solution to the conflict through dialogue and diplomacy. They expressed the expectation that current efforts will lead to a sustainable peace agreement."

a6027.speaker: Brazilian presidency communiqué (BRICS chair statement)
a6027.name: Brazilian presidency communiqué (BRICS chair statement)
a6027.speech: On Gaza, indicated that the "ministers expressed grave concern about the situation in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, about the resumption of Israeli attacks against Gaza and about the obstruction of the entry of humanitarian aid into the territory."

a6106.speaker: Diplomats posted in Washington (anonymous)
a6106.name: Diplomats posted in Washington (anonymous)
a6106.speech: For the diplomats in post, it is an unprecedented diplomatic success, tradition having assigned the State Department responsibility for this type of partnership.

a6354.speaker: Anders Arborelius, Swedish Cardinal
a6354.name: Anders Arborelius
a6354.title: Swedish Cardinal
a6354.speech: Said on Monday he expects this conclave may take longer, as many of the cardinals appointed by Pope Francis have never met each other before. “We don't know each other,” Arborelius, one of about 135 cardinals under the age of 80 who will enter the conclave, said.

a6354.speaker: Walter Kasper, German Cardinal
a6354.name: Walter Kasper
a6354.title: German Cardinal
a6354.speech: Told La Repubblica newspaper that the outpouring of mourners for Francis indicated that Catholics wanted the next pope to continue with his reforming style of papacy. “The People of God voted with their feet,” said Kasper, who is 92 and will not take part in the conclave. “I am convinced that we must go ahead in the footsteps of Francis.”

a6525.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberia's Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a6525.name: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan
a6525.title: Liberia's Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a6525.speech: Called on all Liberians to unite for the country's development and growth, emphasizing that development must transcend political and social divisions: “We call on our people to unite for development” ; “The MCC brings all of us together, no matter your political party or religious connection – that's why we say Liberia wins.”

a6525.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberia's Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a6525.name: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan
a6525.title: Liberia's Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a6525.speech: Reflecting on the positive impact of the first MCC Compact, highlighted tangible benefits such as increased access to electricity from the Mount Coffee Hydro Dam and improved water distribution through the Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation: “The electricity and water provided by the Mount Coffee Hydro Dam and the Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation are beneficial to everyone who gets access. No one needs to show a political party ID card to benefit” ; also acknowledged the significant contributions made by both current and past government officials and technicians in securing Liberia's partnership with the MCC.

a6525.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberia's Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a6525.name: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan
a6525.title: Liberia's Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a6525.speech: Emphasized the importance of prioritizing the needs of the Liberian people, ensuring that development continues regardless of the political cycle: “Election years are when politicians win, but the Liberian people need to win every year.” ; “We win when people in government, the private sector, and everywhere else deliver on the expectations of their people” ; “Our people need roads, more electricity, healthcare, and education – that's how they win.”

a6525.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberia's Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a6525.name: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan
a6525.title: Liberia's Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a6525.speech: Assured the delegation and the Liberian people that efforts are underway to complete a constraint analysis, which will guide the allocation of MCC funding to critical areas of development, and reaffirmed Liberia's commitment to working closely with the MCC to ensure that Compact II will bring long-term benefits to the nation.

a6525.speaker: Jason Small, MCC Managing Director for Africa and head of the delegation
a6525.name: Jason Small
a6525.title: MCC Managing Director for Africa and head of the delegation
a6525.speech: Expressed enthusiasm and commitment to advancing the preparations for Liberia's Compact II, spoke directly to the importance of the partnership between the MCC and Liberia, noting the shared dedication to improving the lives of the Liberian people, and emphasized the MCC's readiness to collaborate closely with the Liberian government to move forward with the compact process: “I know you and your team are very anxious to get moving on the compact, and that's why we're here” ; “We will talk on the long road ahead, close it together, and develop a compact that will transform the lives of the people of Liberia.”

a6525.speaker: Mark Toner, US Ambassador to Liberia
a6525.name: Mark Toner
a6525.title: US Ambassador to Liberia
a6525.speech: Voiced strong support for the ongoing preparations for Liberia's MCC Compact II, emphasizing the importance of the partnership between the U.S. government, the MCC, and Liberia, and the value of fostering close cooperation between the two nations in advancing Liberia's development goals: “This is a real win for Liberia, and we are so pleased that the MCC Delegation can come to network with the Government of Liberia.”

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said Article 67 of the 1992 Constitution requires the President to address the people of Ghana, in whom sovereignty resides, on the state of the nation ; recalled that about thirty years ago, in 1996, he took his first steps in public service when he was elected to the house as Member of Parliament for the Bole Bamboi Constituency, and that God almighty, providence and the unpredictability of life have summoned him here once again on the back of a historic electoral mandate from the people of Ghana.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Conveyed his heartfelt gratitude to Parliament for the prompt vetting and approval of his nominees for Ministerial positions, saying this efficiency is unmatched in the history of the Fourth Republic ; said he trusts the significant reduction to sixty (60) Ministers and Deputy Ministers, including Regional Ministers, will set the stage for further reductions in the size of future governments, and that he intends to significantly reduce the number of Presidency staff compared to the previous administration, all aimed at leading by example in cutting down government expenditures and reducing the budget deficit.

a6568.speaker: John Oatman Jr., hymnist
a6568.name: John Oatman Jr.
a6568.title: hymnist
a6568.speech: Encourages us to count our blessings and name them one by one.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said that yes, we are a nation troubled on many fronts, but we have many blessings, among which is a now firmly established democracy that, for all its imperfections, has enabled four peaceful transfers of power, and that nestled in a sub-region often plagued by strife and political instability there is good reason to take sober satisfaction that these successive peaceful power transfers have become routine.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said that as required by Article 67 he must give an account of the State of the Nation, and reported: "I am sad to report that the state of our nation is not good. Our economy is in crisis, and our people are suffering unprecedented hardships." ; announced that a National Economic Dialogue will be hosted on March 3rd and 4th and that on March 11th the Minister for Finance will, on his behalf, present the budget estimates for the financial year, allowing the real state of Ghana's economic crisis to be presented to the people.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said it is not his style to lament and shift blame when confronted with challenges, as others often do, but to accept challenges and work hard to resolve them, which is precisely what the people of Ghana elected him to do.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Recalled that yesterday, February 26, 2025, marked exactly ten years since he stood in the chamber to declare his determination to fix Dumsor, a legacy problem of power shortages, and said "And I fixed it!", placing firmly on record that from January 2016 until he handed over on January 7, 2017 there was no power rationing or load management in Ghana ; declared that "I, John Dramani Mahama, will fix the economic crisis confronting our country and reset it on a path of growth and prosperity."

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said that nothing could prepare anyone for the reality of the depths to which the economy and governance have sunk, that after an initial assessment of the books the economic problems are much deeper than was publicly known, and that the country is saddled with staggering debts and glaring signs of almost deliberate and, in some cases, criminal mismanagement of resources ; said not even the restraints of an IMF programme were enough for the previous economic managers to exercise prudence, noting inflation of 23.8% against an 18% target, the cedi losing 19% of its value against the dollar in 2024 after 27.8% in 2023, public debt of GH¢721 billion, ECG's debt of GH¢68 billion, COCOBOD's total debt of GH¢32.5 billion, an energy sector financing shortfall of about US$2.2 billion (GHS 34 billion) for 2025, GH¢29.9 billion spent on the financial sector clean-up, a Sinking Fund balance of only $64,000 and GH¢143 million, GH¢280 billion of debt servicing over the next four years, and 55 stalled projects with US$2.95 billion not disbursed and expected cost overruns of about GH¢15 billion.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said COCOBOD could not supply 333,767 tonnes of cocoa sold at US$2,600 per tonne in the 2023/2024 crop season, so the then management rolled the contracts over into 2024/2025, meaning COCOBOD and the Ghanaian farmer lose US$4,000 in revenue for every tonne delivered against the rolled-over contracts - a revenue loss of US$840 million on the 210,000 tonnes already supplied and another US$495 million to come - and that cocoa road commitments alone total GH¢21.7 billion, arising mainly because of the decision in 2019 and 2020 to award road contracts worth over US$1 billion because of the election.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said he remains committed to leading the government and taking every necessary step to reset the economy, that the government is doubling efforts to complete all outstanding structural reforms and will implement corrective measures through the budget to restore fiscal discipline and debt sustainability, that the fourth review of the IMF-supported Programme is scheduled from April 2 to April 15, 2025 with Executive Board approval expected in June 2025, and that buffers are being built in the Sinking Fund ; reported the government honoured matured coupon payments of GH¢6.081 billion in cash and GH¢3.46 billion in kind due in February 2025 to Domestic Debt Exchange Programme bondholders ; urged his countrymen and women, business owners and foreign investors to trust the government's competence in turning economic fortunes around.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said that since taking office on January 7, 2025 the government has upheld its commitment to a fiscal consolidation agenda with a streamlined government, eliminated unnecessary expenditures and reduced reliance on borrowing, and that prudent debt management has led to a substantial reduction in interest rates, with the 91-day treasury bill rate falling from 28.51% to 24.48%, the 182-day rate from 29.07% to 25.388% and the 364-day rate from 30.41% to 27.30% between January 6 and February 24, 2025 ; said a Memorandum of Understanding was signed with the Official Creditor Committee to formalise the agreed debt treatment, a crucial step toward restoring long-term debt sustainability.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Reiterated his sincere gratitude to Organised Labour and the Ghana Employers Association for their understanding and cooperation in reaching agreement on the 2025 minimum wage and base pay, concluded on February 20, 2025 by the National Tripartite Committee and the Public Services Joint Standing Negotiating Committee, and said he is confident the sacrifice all have to make this year will significantly benefit the economy's health ; said the country looks forward to a positive economic outlook as it restores macroeconomic stability, encourages exports, activates the 24-Hour Economy initiative, implements the US$10 billion 'Big Push' policy for swift infrastructure development, rationalises taxes and fosters inclusive growth, with the goal being prosperity for all, shared and not the prerogative of a select few.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said that in fulfilment of the 120-day social contract a planning committee has been put in place to host the National Economic Dialogue, which will discuss the state of the economy, reach consensus on key policies, support a home-grown fiscal consolidation programme and highlight key structural reforms ; expressed hope that colleagues on the other side of the divide will display love of country and participate, unlike their boycott of the Senchi Forum in 2014, and said he humbly chooses a different path of accommodation and cooperation with all stakeholders.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said his administration inherited an energy sector on the brink of collapse weighed down by unsustainable debts, leading many Independent Power Producers and fuel suppliers to threaten to cease operations, and that despite collecting over GHS 45 billion in Energy Sector Levies over the last eight years the outgone NPP administration left an energy sector burdened with a staggering GH¢70 billion debt as of December 2024 ; said critical maintenance such as the scheduled pigging of the West African Gas Pipeline was postponed from 2024 to 2025 without sufficient contingency measures, forcing his administration to swiftly mobilise emergency fuel supplies, and that once the pigging is completed in the first weeks of March and additional gas flows from Nigeria a marked improvement in the power situation is anticipated ; said he has directed the Minister for Energy and Green Transitions to implement far-reaching reforms including enforcing a single revenue collection account, strictly adhering to the Cash Waterfall Mechanism and eliminating wasteful expenditures, cited the successful ECG-Enclave Power pilot as a workable framework, and said the administration will soon operationalise a Renewable Energy and Green Transition Fund and aims in the medium term to achieve 100% gas utilisation for power production and eliminate the use of crude oil.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said Ghana's petroleum sector has witnessed a precipitous decline with crude oil production shrinking by more than 32%, resulting from high opacity levels, a hostile business climate and excessive political interference that caused most major oil companies to exit and stalled upstream activities, and that his recent visit to Sekondi-Takoradi revealed many shut down facilities and businesses that have packed and left, with hundreds of workers laid off ; assured the people of Sekondi-Takoradi and the whole Western Region that the government will breathe life back into the area, and said meetings with players in the upstream sector have been extremely positive with assurances of substantial investments running into billions of dollars in the very near future.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said Ghana has fertile lands, abundant water and human resources yet faces a paradox, with the food import bill soaring to over US$2 billion annually and rising food inflation burdening households ; announced the Agriculture for Economic Transformation Agenda (AETA), the Feed Ghana Programme with its Grains and Vegetable Development Projects, a poultry farm-to-table project and the Nkoko nkitinkiti project covering 55,000 households to help eliminate poultry imports that cost over US$300 million annually, the AgriNext Programme benefiting approximately 30,000 young people, the Livestock Development Project, Farmer Service Centres in every agricultural district, continued enforcement of measures to curb illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, expanded supply of subsidised premix fuel, investment in modern fish landing sites and cold storage, aquaculture support and programmes to empower female fish processors and traders.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said that one of the biggest crises the country faces is youth unemployment, with the latest estimates showing up to two million youth unemployed, posing a major security risk requiring urgent attention ; said he has set up the Ministry for Youth Development and Empowerment in furtherance of his campaign promise ; announced the Adwumawura Programme supporting the top 2,000 implementable business proposals, a flagship National Apprenticeship Programme to equip 10,000 young people in the informal sector, training and electric motorcycles on hire purchase for young people in the okada business, the Vice-President's Empowerment for Women and People with Disabilities Programme, and the 'One Million Coders Programme'.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said that as part of the Operation Recover All Loot policy he has already tasked investigative bodies to bring the culprits of the National Service ghost names scandal to justice, that such brazen theft of public funds must be stopped and punished, that the criminal addition of more than 80,000 ghost names could have yielded the suspects over GH¢50 million a month, and that as some suspects are believed to have absconded he has directed that they be declared wanted and their assets traced and frozen until investigations are completed ; said he has tasked the Minister for Youth Development and Empowerment to present to Parliament a Legislative Instrument to support implementation of the National Service Authority Act 2024 (Act 1119), and that short military training will be introduced as part of the national service scheme.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said the administration of scholarships has been fraught with challenges, with the poor who genuinely need scholarships unable to access them because the rich always crowd them out, and that the award process will be streamlined with increased transparency including publishing the list of beneficiaries every year.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said issues related to low learning outcomes persist within Ghana's educational system and the system inherited is outdated in many ways and must be realigned to meet the needs of the 21st century and the Fourth Industrial Revolution ; said he launched the National Education Consultative Forum on February 18 in Ho and looks forward to the recommendations ; announced that basic education will be redefined with a "Zero to Hero" initiative for foundational literacy and numeracy, ICT training integrated into early childhood education expanding over three years to 300 classrooms, 30 centres of excellence and 1,000 teachers, full implementation of a new curriculum for Senior High Technical and STEM Schools, a standardised National Sign Language, scaled-up Capitation Grants and feeding grants, measures to promote inclusion and equity including the Islamic Education Unit and STEM and TVET schools in underserved peri-urban communities, plans for a 20% allowance for teachers serving in rural schools and construction of teacher accommodation under the Teacher Dabr3 initiative.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Stated "once again for emphasis, and for the record, I, John Dramani Mahama, President of the Republic of Ghana, will not cancel the free SHS programme. I am determined to make it better by improving its implementation." ; said that for the record students who have benefitted from free SHS since its inception are about 3.4 million and that the figure of 5.1 million beneficiaries previously put out by the Akufo-Addo government "was an exaggerated and false narrative calculated to achieve political credit" ; said that while it has improved access, the implementation of free SHS leaves much to be desired and the outcomes of the ongoing National Education Forum will guide reforms ; said the double-track system remains a challenge and the government is committed to eliminating it by accelerating school infrastructure expansion and completing stalled projects, with the Education and Finance Ministries working to uncap the GETFund.

a6568.speaker: Minister for Education of Ghana
a6568.name: Minister for Education of Ghana
a6568.speech: Has announced the restoration of Parent-Teacher Associations (PTAs), in line with the government's promise.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said Ghana has consistently missed its Gross Tertiary Enrolment targets, with the rate below 22% against the 40% goal by 2030, and that of over 460,000 secondary graduates annually 55% qualify for tertiary education but only 35% (161,000) enrol, leaving over 300,000 without access ; said government is introducing a no-fee stress policy to eliminate tertiary admission fees, supported by an enhanced Student Loan Scheme (Student Loan Plus), covering all Persons with Disabilities who gain admission, and that TVET enrolment will be increased from 11% to 20% ; said feasibility studies for new public universities or campuses in the six new regions will commence this year with seed funding from the GETFund, that private sector participation in hostel provision will be pursued on university lands, and that academic freedom will be upheld.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said the health sector faces significant challenges that jeopardize the very foundation of the health system, with the Ministry of Health carrying a total liability of nearly GH¢15 billion when co-financing obligations, judgment debts and payments to clear medical commodities at the ports are combined, and that the last major hospital equipment replacement programme was undertaken in 2014 when he was President, since when most hospital equipment in GHS facilities has deteriorated or broken down ; said the Agenda 111 programme started as a knee-jerk reaction during the COVID-19 pandemic, that the promise was to build 111 hospitals but no dedicated funding source was secured, that "as I speak, not a single Agenda 111 hospital is operational in any part of Ghana", that US$400 million has already been disbursed which at about $18m per hospital could have completed at least 22 hospitals, and that GH¢22 billion will now be required to complete the projects ; said he has tasked the Minister for Health to present a plan on the way forward and that the government is open to public-private partnerships and franchising.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said that one of the most pressing issues confronting the health sector is USAID's sudden 90-day pause in services without prior notice and the looming threat of complete withdrawal of programmes that do not align with the USA's strategic interests ; said the programmes affected include the delivery of medical commodities to regional medical stores and health facilities in the Upper West, Upper East, Northern and Savannah regions, and USAID's support for the National HIV/AIDS Control Programme including the supply of antiretroviral therapies in the Western, Western North and Ahafo Regions ; said the withdrawal puts at risk approximately $78 million earmarked for malaria, maternal and child health, nutrition and HIV/AIDS programmes and that "the impact will be devastating without urgent intervention" ; said he has therefore directed the Minister for Finance to make immediate financial arrangements to mitigate this loss and expects this to be reflected in the budget to be presented next month.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said that working with the NHIA the government will revive the ONUADOR mobile healthcare vans to provide OPD, ophthalmology, dental, ENT and cancer screening care in remote and vulnerable communities, an earlier attempt having been abandoned after the change of government in 2017.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said public health experts are grappling with new diseases and the re-emergence of old diseases and that the health system must be made resilient to shocks ; reported that since October last year Ghana has faced a severe cholera outbreak, with 6,300 suspected cases, 545 confirmed cases and 49 deaths as of February 17, 2025 across 118 districts in Greater Accra, Central, Western, Ashanti and Eastern Regions, and that an aggressive vaccination and public education campaign has been launched ; reported that the Upper West Region is facing a severe meningitis outbreak with 135 suspected cases, 22 confirmed cases and 16 deaths across ten districts as of February 17, 2025, that free treatment has been instituted and a national team of health experts deployed ; said sanitation, personal hygiene and environmental sanitation must be a major priority and committed to keeping communities and cities clean through appropriate investments, supervision and performance tracking.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said his administration is actively developing the framework for the rollout of the Free Primary Healthcare Programme, which when fully implemented will mark a significant step towards achieving SDG Goal 3.8 on universal health coverage by eliminating financial barriers ; said the technical committee for the Ghana Medical Trust Fund (MahamaCare) is far advanced with plans to establish it in the coming weeks, dedicated to financing treatment of non-communicable diseases including dialysis and cancer care, with government allocating resources in 2025 and further support to be mobilised from private sector partners.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said that as a Social Democrat he is resolutely committed to eradicating all forms of discrimination, and that with Vice President Prof. Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang the government will engage all stakeholders including development partners and civil society organisations to prioritise gender equality, equity and social justice, establish strong social protection mechanisms and enhance legal safeguards for women, girls and other vulnerable groups ; commended the Speaker for his support in passing the Affirmative Action Act, 2024 (Act 1121) and said his government is dedicated to implementing it, including attaining the 30% target quota for women in political appointments, reporting that women currently make up 23.21% of all appointments ; said he is concerned about gender balance at local government level and hopes the National Constitution Review Conference will clear a pathway for the election of DCEs ; announced the establishment of the Women's Development Bank with initial funding to be allocated in the upcoming Budget, and the expansion of the Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty programme under the "Big LEAP" initiative ; committed to passing the Persons with Disability (Amendment) Bill, free tertiary education for persons with disabilities and implementation of the 5% employment reservation for persons with disabilities.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said Ghana's sports sector, once a shining example of excellence within Africa, now finds itself at a critical juncture, with recent years unveiling pressing structural deficiencies in administration, funding, infrastructure and talent development that make immediate and comprehensive reforms imperative ; announced a comprehensive National Sports Policy, a review of the Sports Act of 2016 (Act 934), enforcement of the Sports Regulations 2023 (LI 2477), refurbishment of national stadiums, the establishment of a School Sports Authority, the renaming of the ministry to the Ministry of Sports and Recreation and the launch of a National Recreation Day and annual National Recreation Festival ; said he has instructed his Office and the Minister to hold the Ghana Football Association accountable to the people of Ghana ahead of the Black Stars' two World Cup qualifying matches, especially regarding the budget the FA has presented, and that "there will be no secrecy in how much the government spends on the national teams."

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts remain vital cornerstones of national development, and announced the flagship 'THE BLACK STAR EXPERIENCE' initiative to establish Ghana as the gateway to Africa for the global diaspora, including a Pan African Month with street carnivals, film week, a fashion festival, a food fair and domestic tourism destinations, the strategic promotion of MICE tourism, the revitalisation of the Accra Marine Drive Project covering approximately 241 acres of Accra's coastline which stalled under the previous administration, and the development of the Osu Castle and its surroundings as a tourist attraction.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said the road network is the cornerstone of the nation's infrastructure, facilitating over 90% of the transportation of goods and services ; said that while the previous government made lofty claims about achieving "unprecedented milestones", available evidence does not support its assertion that it constructed over 13,000 kilometres of new roads, and that it has perpetuated a narrative presenting road maintenance and rehabilitation as new construction, misleading the public ; said the proportion of poor roads increased in urban areas from 46% in 2015 to 57% by 2021, that the road sector is in crisis mainly due to years of mismanagement with as many as 85% of awarded contracts stalled, that unpaid bills owed to contractors exceeded GH¢20 billion as of December 2024 and current commitments for road projects total an astonishing GH¢105 billion ; said the strategy will be anchored in the "Big Push" Programme and that the government will reintroduce tolls using modern technology, rationalise the road sector portfolio, de-cap the Road Fund, minimise sole-source procurement and reorganise the DRIP equipment into regional mobile maintenance units.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said he has realigned the Ministry of Transport to oversee aviation, maritime and inland water transport, road transport and railways ; announced a feasibility study for coastal water transport services, an amendment of the regulatory framework to regularise motorcycles and tricycles ("Okada") for commercial passenger transport, a state-of-the-art pilot training academy and Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul facility at Ho Airport making the Volta Region a centre of excellence for aviation, passenger rail services between Tema and Adome following completion of the Tema-Mpakadan line, continued modernisation of the Western Railway Line in partnership with the private sector, and a transparent expression of interest to establish a national airline after the previous administration's attempt failed.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said Communication and Digital Technology initiatives focus on expanding national digital infrastructure, but that the sector faces insufficient infrastructure for weather and climate services, fragmented and uncoordinated databases, outdated legislation, a lack of adequate cybersecurity technology and a daunting debt burden exceeding GH¢2 billion ; said his government is committed to reviewing existing laws and policies to align them with emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Big Data, the Internet of Things and Machine Learning, and to expediting enactment of the Kofi Annan Centre of Excellence in ICT (KACE) Bill.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said the water sector faces considerable challenges, particularly from illegal mining activities that contaminate freshwater sources, and that government will prioritise completing new and ongoing water projects in communities including Keta, Wenchi, Sekondi-Takoradi, Asankragwa, Sefwi Wiawso, Duadaso, Kweiman Danfa, Goaso, Juaben, Aveyime and Adu Bamso, and tackle critical projects in Damongo, Tamale, Yendi, Sunyani, Techiman and Tarkwa ; said two-thirds of Ghana's approximately 550-kilometre coastline is threatened by tidal wave erosion impacting nearly 30% of the population, that coastal protection has emerged as a national priority, and that alternative funding sources will be explored for drainage, desilting, flood control and coastal protection ; said the housing deficit, estimated at 1.8 million units, has loomed large for years and that the government is committed to completing all ongoing housing initiatives beginning with the Saglemi Affordable Housing Project, and will implement a low-cost Social Housing Project supported by a District Housing Scheme allowing formal sector workers with 15 to 20 years before retirement to purchase a house in cedis with monthly salary deductions.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said illegal mining, commonly known as 'Galamsey', has inflicted tremendous harm on forests, leading to significant land degradation and pollution of vital water sources, with 44 of the country's 288 forest reserves impacted - an area alarmingly equivalent to approximately 7,504 football pitches - and turbidity levels in major rivers within the Southwestern Basin far exceeding permissible limits ; said the response includes robust and impartial law enforcement, meaningful stakeholder engagement, alternative livelihood programmes, expansion of the Minerals Commission's regional offices, a framework categorising mining into small, medium and large-scale operations, and the establishment of a Gold Board ; announced the 'Tree for Life' restoration policy and the Blue Water Initiative, an afforestation programme of 20,000 hectares of new plantations and 5,000 hectares of enrichment planting annually, and policies on critical minerals such as lithium and integrated aluminium and iron industries.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said climate change remains a pressing concern for Ghana and the global community, that Ghana has allocated 24 million metric tonnes of its 64 million metric tonne carbon budget for authorisation under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement and has successfully authorised three projects poised to reduce 5.2 million tonnes of carbon emissions, and that in line with the NDC's 2024 Manifesto the government is committed to strengthening institutional and human capacity for adaptation and mitigation in agriculture, forestry, energy and water resources and to aligning national policies with international efforts to limit global warming to 1.5°C by 2050 and promote a fair and just transition to renewable energy.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said that during his campaign he pledged, as captured by the NDC's 2024 Manifesto, to take a strong stance against corruption, end state capture and end the purchase of State and public assets such as lands by members of the political class, and to fight corruption head-on by implementing Operation Recover All Loot (ORAL) ; announced that the ORAL committee received over two thousand complaints and has submitted a comprehensive report which has been handed to the Attorney General for review, thorough investigation and eventual prosecution, and that the recent arrests related to the unwarranted payment of Two Million US Dollars in the Skytrain saga and the National Service ghost names scandal mark only the beginning ; said a unit will be established at the presidency to receive complaints and reports regarding graft, that a bill will shortly be submitted to regulate and restrict the sale or disposal of public and state assets, and that once the 2025 Budget is approved the government will reform existing anti-corruption agencies, increase funding and improve transparency and accountability.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said delays and uncertainties have plagued justice delivery in Ghana, leading many Ghanaians to perceive a politicisation of the judicial process, with public trust in the judiciary's independence alarmingly low, and that his government will uphold judicial independence, work with the judicial council and services to depoliticise justice delivery and collaborate closely with the Chief Justice to combat corruption ; said a Legal Education Reform Bill has been developed ready for Cabinet approval and laying before Parliament ; said that on January 30, 2025 he inaugurated the Constitution Review Committee, composed of distinguished scholars, jurists and professionals, to engage Ghanaians over the next six months, with findings ultimately presented to the public for approval in a referendum followed by submission to Parliament for enactment.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Reported that Ghana's internal security remains stable despite developments primarily rooted in chieftaincy disputes, and announced comprehensive reforms across all security agencies, a more transparent and equitable recruitment process in response to accusations of politicisation, favouritism and selectivity, and enhanced capabilities for the Ghana Police Service, Prisons Service, Ghana National Fire Service, Immigration Service, Narcotics Control Commission, the Customs Division of the Ghana Revenue Authority and all investigative bodies ; reaffirmed the government's unwavering commitment to prioritising the welfare and well-being of security personnel through investment in adequate equipment and suitable accommodation.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said that as Commander-in-Chief he wants to emphasise the determination to strengthen democracy, particularly given the troubling proliferation of military-grade weapons that fell into unauthorised hands under the previous administration, which pose a significant threat to national security and constitutional democracy, and reported substantial progress in accounting for these unregistered weapons and a commitment to ensuring those responsible are brought to justice ; said the country remains vigilant against violent extremism and terrorism and is resolute in enhancing defence mechanisms through diplomacy, counter-intelligence, information sharing, infrastructure development and acquisition of specialised technologies ; said the Ghana Armed Forces face a housing shortfall of over 17,000 units, that ration and fuel supplies will be improved, that facilities at the 37 Military Hospital will be expanded and the delayed Afari (Kumasi) Military Hospital completed and operationalised before the end of the year ; said the Ministry of Defence is burdened with approximately GH¢3.7 billion in debt, a figure that continues to grow as new undisclosed debts are uncovered, and that he has tasked the Minister for Defence with incorporating innovation and significant private sector participation into the Defence Industries Holding Company (DIHOC).

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said Ghana's strong international reputation was reaffirmed by the historic participation of foreign leaders at the swearing-in on January 7, 2025, reflecting confidence in the country's stability and democratic progress, and that Ghana remains committed to Pan-Africanism, non-alignment, democracy and global cooperation, embracing a "friends to all and enemies to none policy" ; said "Ghana is open for business" and that the policy on economic diplomacy focuses on export diversification, foreign investment and job creation, with a new blueprint and delivery unit at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs with clear Key Performance Indicators to be launched soon ; said that because of emerging security threats, especially on the borders, Ghana is committed to security initiatives particularly in the Sahel, will maintain continuous engagement with Sahelian neighbours and has appointed a Special Envoy to help sustain diplomatic relations and achieve their reintegration into the regional bloc ; said passport application centres will be expanded nationwide to reduce processing times to 7 days.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said the government will revamp labour administration institutions, promote social dialogue and foster harmonious industrial relations, and that in the coming months the National Tripartite Committee will organise a National Labour Conference whose recommendations are expected to shape government policies ; said the government will maintain strict fiduciary responsibility for the National Pensions Regulatory Authority and SSNIT, that the NPRA will fully automate its internal operations this year, and that an Informal Sector Pension Inclusion Initiative will be implemented to increase participation in micro pension schemes beyond the current 11% coverage ; said key players in decentralisation such as Assemblymen and women often face neglect and inadequate compensation and reaffirmed his commitment to the promise to pay them modest allowances.

a6568.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6568.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6568.title: President of Ghana
a6568.speech: Said he has unveiled the State of the Nation as he met it along with measures to address the inherited challenges, but that no matter how well-intentioned they will not yield the desired outcome without the support of the people of Ghana ; told his countrymen and women that they had clearly and unmistakably expressed their displeasure with the previous government's poor governance, some even at the peril of their lives like the 28th February Crossroads Shooting National Heroes, and that "the arrogance of power you so much abhor will be a thing of the past" ; admitted that "the entire economic value chain is indeed in the ICU", as he recalled mentioning a few years ago while in opposition, and that the economy is even worse than envisaged but this gives ample opportunity to be innovative ; listed the takeaways for the people of Ghana as fighting corruption effectively, running a lean government of not more than 60 Ministers, realignment of ministries, agencies and departments, introducing austerity and reducing wasteful expenditure while improving tax collections, widening the tax net and reforming tax waivers, and growing what the country eats to reduce imports of food and goods that can easily be produced at home ; committed to the judicious use of the people's resources and eschewing waste and ostentation, said Ghana's economic challenges are not insurmountable and present an opportunity to innovate, Reflect, Review and Reset - the theme for the 68th Independence Anniversary - and closed by saying "where despair once existed, hope must radiate" and that when next he stands to present a message on the State of the Nation "it will be one brimming with evidence of progress."

a6658.speaker: Internal planning documents seen by Reuters
a6658.name: Internal planning documents seen by Reuters
a6658.speech: According to internal planning documents seen by Reuters, the White House budget office has proposed eliminating funding for United Nations peacekeeping missions, citing failures by operations in Mali, Lebanon and Democratic Republic of Congo.

a6658.speaker: Tammy Bruce, State Department spokesperson
a6658.name: Tammy Bruce
a6658.title: State Department spokesperson
a6658.speech: "There is no final plan, final budget," she told reporters on Tuesday when asked about the OMB proposals.

a6658.speaker: Office of Management and Budget "Passback" document
a6658.name: Office of Management and Budget "Passback" document
a6658.speech: Proposed ending Contributions for International Peacekeeping Activities (CIPA): "For example, Passback provides no funding for CIPA, ending contributions for international peacekeeping due to the recent failures in peacekeeping, such as with MINUSMA, UNIFIL, and MONUSCO, and the disproportionately high level of assessments."

a6658.speaker: Office of Management and Budget "Passback" document
a6658.name: Office of Management and Budget "Passback" document
a6658.speech: Proposed the creation of a $2.1 billion America First Opportunities Fund (A1OF), which it said would be used to cover a limited set of foreign economic and development assistance priorities: "Should the Administration seek to pay any assessments for the United Nations Regular Budget or peacekeeping assessments, we would look to provide that funding from the A1OF."

a6658.speaker: Stephane Dujarric, U.N. spokesperson
a6658.name: Stephane Dujarric
a6658.title: U.N. spokesperson
a6658.speech: On Tuesday declined to comment on "what appears to be a leaked memo that is part of an internal debate within the U.S. government."

a6658.speaker: Antonio Guterres, U.N. Secretary-General
a6658.name: Antonio Guterres
a6658.title: U.N. Secretary-General
a6658.speech: Last month said he is seeking ways to improve efficiency and cut costs as the world body turns 80 this year amid a cash crisis.

a6757.speaker: Duma Boko, President of Botswana
a6757.name: Duma Boko
a6757.title: President of Botswana
a6757.speech: Announced the public health emergency in a televised address on Monday, setting out a multimillion-dollar plan to rectify the supply chain involving military oversight; said managing the shortages would be "highly price sensitive due to our limited coffers" ; "The work shall remain nonstop until the entire value chain of procurement has been fixed," announcing that the finance ministry had approved 250m pula (£13.8m, $18.3m) in emergency funding.

a6757.speaker: Duma Boko, President of Botswana
a6757.name: Duma Boko
a6757.title: President of Botswana
a6757.speech: Before taking office, he said his main focus would be to fix an economy too reliant on diamonds.

a6757.speaker: Botswana health ministry
a6757.name: Botswana health ministry
a6757.speech: Earlier this month, said that it was facing "significant challenges", including medical shortages and debts of more than 1bn pula (£55.2m), the bulk of which was due to patients being admitted to private hospitals for services that were not publicly available; also temporarily suspended referrals for elective surgeries and non-urgent medical conditions, including organ transplant surgeries.

a6757.speaker: Dr Stephen Modise, Health Minister of Botswana
a6757.name: Dr Stephen Modise
a6757.title: Health Minister of Botswana
a6757.speech: Listed shortages including medicines and supplies for managing cancers, HIV treatments and tuberculosis among others ; said: "I have no doubt that soon, very soon, we will overcome. This is definitely not insurmountable."

a6757.speaker: UNAIDS
a6757.name: UNAIDS
a6757.speech: According to UNAIDS, before the cuts to US aid issued by President Donald Trump, the US funded a third of Botswana's HIV response.

a6757.speaker: Unicef (UN children's agency)
a6757.name: Unicef (UN children's agency)
a6757.speech: Has called for "urgent action" in the country to "protect the health and future of every child in Botswana"; noted that "malnutrition is a daily struggle" in the town of D'Kar, saying "the president's call underscores what we witness on the ground".

a6757.speaker: Reuters news agency
a6757.name: Reuters news agency
a6757.speech: Reported that as part of the military's distribution efforts, the first trucks were due to leave the capital, Gaborone, on Monday and arrive in remote areas by the evening.

a6770.speaker: Botswana Energy Regulatory Authority (BERA)
a6770.name: Botswana Energy Regulatory Authority (BERA)
a6770.speech: Has announced discontinuation of the sale and use of unleaded petrol 93 (ULP 93) in Botswana with effect from 1st February 2025 ; says the short supply of the popular petrol grade will persist because most refineries that supply Botswana with it have shut down in recent months ; according to BERA, the decline in South Africa's refining capacity is due to the state of the refineries that require upgrading and repairing in order to produce cleaner fuel supply.

a6770.speaker: Botswana Energy Regulatory Authority (BERA) (statement)
a6770.name: Botswana Energy Regulatory Authority (BERA) (statement)
a6770.speech: "Regionally ULP 93 is produced in limited quantities only in South Africa at the NATREF Refinery. This refinery is the main source for the ULP 93 imported into Botswana and other countries in the region. Although there may be ULP 93 through some sporadic imports from other regions of the world and possibly into South Africa, there are currently challenges with such products being re-exported owing to the South African Revenue Services (SARS) rules."

a6770.speaker: Botswana Energy Regulatory Authority (BERA) (statement signed by Acting CEO Pelaelo Kgomotso)
a6770.name: Botswana Energy Regulatory Authority (BERA) (statement signed by Acting CEO Pelaelo Kgomotso)
a6770.speech: Dismissed the notion that ULP 93 gives vehicles more mileage than ULP 95 and encouraged the public to embrace the readily available ULP 95: "The Authority would like to assure the public that the discontinuation of ULP 93 will not adversely affect them since all petrol engines can run on unleaded petrol 95 (ULP 95), which is in abundance and readily available both regionally and internationally. Infact, ULP 95 is a better-quality product compared to ULP 93 which is an older grade."

a6770.speaker: Botswana Oil Limited (BOL)
a6770.name: Botswana Oil Limited (BOL)
a6770.speech: According to information provided by Botswana Oil Limited, ULP 93 is the most consumed petrol grade in Botswana.

a6856.speaker: Voices in the Burundian basketball world (unnamed)
a6856.name: Voices in the Burundian basketball world (unnamed)
a6856.speech: “Why so many businessmen for a training camp?” ; “Is this really about promoting young Burundian basketball players, or about promoting a handful of businessmen devoted to his cause?” Since the official announcement of the list of staff members making the trip, questions and indignation have erupted from every corner of the basketball world.

a6856.speaker: Some internet users (social media commenters)
a6856.name: Some internet users (social media commenters)
a6856.speech: Maintain that it is “further proof that the current president of the Burundi Basketball Federation (Febabu) is driven only by commercial aims rather than by the development of basketball.”

a6856.speaker: Some club supporters interviewed (unnamed)
a6856.name: Some club supporters interviewed (unnamed)
a6856.speech: Highly critical, they do not understand why there is no member of the commission in charge of youth development within Febabu: “Since this is about acquiring new knowledge and sharing experience, the least they could have done was give a chance to a technical staff member who belongs to that commission, the one that conducted the selections.”

a6856.speaker: Franck, former player and club staff member in the Association of Clubs
a6856.name: Franck
a6856.title: former player and club staff member in the Association of Clubs
a6856.speech: For him, this reflects the Febabu president’s tendency to listen only to his own voice.

a6856.speaker: Some members of Febabu’s executive board (unnamed)
a6856.name: Some members of Febabu’s executive board (unnamed)
a6856.speech: Confirm that they were not consulted for their approval of the delegation members who will be making the trip.

a6856.speaker: Fernand, former player
a6856.name: Fernand
a6856.title: former player
a6856.speech: Wonders: “What will happen when the association that invited him discovers that their partner is no longer a showcase of young players, but rather of businessmen?” For him, the competent authorities must realise that such practices risk tarnishing Burundi’s image.

a6856.speaker: Aimé Bitagoye, coach of Remesha club and member of Febabu’s youth development commission
a6856.name: Aimé Bitagoye
a6856.title: coach of Remesha club and member of Febabu’s youth development commission
a6856.speech: Says he was surprised that no member of their commission was included, but that in no way “does this weaken our determination to contribute to the rebirth of Burundian basketball by training young talent.”

a6856.speaker: Lionel Banyiyezako, Febabu spokesman
a6856.name: Lionel Banyiyezako
a6856.title: Febabu spokesman
a6856.speech: “False!” he retorts to claims that Febabu is extracting money from parents; specifies that the sum of 11 million BIF was set after consultation with the parents’ committee, and says that contrary to the malicious tongues demonising the Febabu president, everything is written down in black and white, with the line items for which the 11 million will be used — besides the plane ticket, travel insurance, camp registration fees, and so on.

a6856.speaker: Lionel Banyiyezako, Febabu spokesman
a6856.name: Lionel Banyiyezako
a6856.title: Febabu spokesman
a6856.speech: On allegations that Febabu president Jean-Paul Manirakiza favours certain businessmen, denounces a campaign of lies: “Whether they like it or not, the rebirth is under way and the results are already tangible. People may of course wonder why no technical coach was retained to be part of the trip. But it is not matches that our young players will be playing. It is a training camp with seasoned tacticians. The objective is to see whether our players have the prerequisites needed to compete in their own championships” ; “As for the choice of the staff members who will make the trip, one single consideration prevailed. The people on the list are officials in certain clubs before being businessmen. Directly or indirectly, in their activities they give considerable support to Febabu.” ; indicates the objective is to allow them to make new contacts and draw inspiration from the experience of American investors in order to raise the level of Burundian basketball: “The partnership with Ballers Paradise will last 5 years. During that period, in addition to other partnerships in the pipeline, we hope to send as many technical staff abroad as possible to strengthen their capacities.”

a6856.speaker: One of the parents interviewed (anonymous)
a6856.name: One of the parents interviewed (anonymous)
a6856.speech: Confides that the amount is enormous for a trip on which accommodation and subsistence are covered: “Since we were clearly told that anyone unable to pay this amount would be removed from the list even if selected, we had no choice but to accept, especially as it is our children’s future that is at stake.”

a6856.speaker: Officials of Ballers Paradise (non-response)
a6856.name: Officials of Ballers Paradise (non-response)
a6856.speech: “We contacted the officials of Ballers Paradise, without success.”

a6953.speaker: South Africa (host of the G20 meeting)
a6953.name: South Africa (host of the G20 meeting)
a6953.speech: Voiced dismay on Thursday that the Group of 20 talks it hosted on global economic issues ended without consensus, after top officials from several countries skipped it and delegates remained far apart on issues such as climate finance.

a6953.speaker: G20 chair's summary issued by the host, South Africa
a6953.name: G20 chair's summary issued by the host
a6953.title: South Africa
a6953.speech: Said participants "reiterated the commitment to resisting protectionism" and had "supported a rules-based, non-discriminatory, fair, open, inclusive, equitable, sustainable and transparent multilateral trading system"; noted on the global economy that growth patterns varied across economies and that various risks and trends had been discussed ; "Inflation has receded, supported by well-calibrated monetary policies and the unwinding of supply shocks, although progress has varied across countries."

a6953.speaker: Enoch Godongwana, South African Finance Minister
a6953.name: Enoch Godongwana
a6953.title: South African Finance Minister
a6953.speech: Said he was "not happy" the G20 meeting could not issue a joint communique ; "I'm not going to (name) ... any specific country, but climate issues are becoming a challenge for the first time" ; "I think there is a view that we should prioritise other things than necessary climate financing," he told Reuters after issuing the G20 summary ; in an earlier news conference he said that though there was a difference of opinion on the way forward on climate action, "there has been general agreement against protectionism and economic fragmentation."

a6953.speaker: Kazuo Ueda, Bank of Japan Governor
a6953.name: Kazuo Ueda
a6953.title: Bank of Japan Governor
a6953.speech: Told reporters after the meeting that "the broader G20 view was that if downside risks like geopolitical tension and supply chain disruptions materialize, that could hamper the G20 goal of achieving sustainable, balanced global growth."

a7038.speaker: Kgosientsho Ramokgopa, Minister of Electricity
a7038.name: Kgosientsho Ramokgopa
a7038.title: Minister of Electricity
a7038.speech: Said at his weekly briefing on the energy action plan that the lower stages of load shedding over the past week are due, in part, to improved plant performance as well as lower winter maintenance and lower demand; that the Eskom board had hoped to reach an average of 60% EAF by 31 March and that, given the unpredictability of the Eskom plant, it is too early to assume a permanent improvement; and that unplanned losses or breakdowns have decreased over the past week from 18 000MW to around 16 000MW, which still means close to a third of Eskom's plant is not functioning due to breakdown.

a7038.speaker: Kgosientsho Ramokgopa, Minister of Electricity
a7038.name: Kgosientsho Ramokgopa
a7038.title: Minister of Electricity
a7038.speech: Reported that work was under way to improve logistics at the open-cycle gas turbine plants to enable more diesel to be moved, stored and burnt, with the aim of increasing the load factor of the turbines to 15% from around 10%; that Nersa had given the go-ahead for Eskom to proceed with the construction of new solar PV at three existing power stations and battery storage at one and was also expected to approve several cross-border purchases soon, including 80MW from a power ship moored off Mozambique, with prospects that more energy could be procured from Mozambique; and that more than 1 000MW of private power generation projects were in the connection phase, with a further 13 000MW at the Eskom “budget quote” stage.

a7038.speaker: Eric Shunmagum, Eskom manager
a7038.name: Eric Shunmagum
a7038.title: Eskom manager
a7038.speech: Said in an update on the state of the system that while breakdowns were lower than the trend, demand was also lower than Eskom had expected at just over 29 000MW against the 30 000MW that had been expected, that the cold fronts had also brought very good performance from wind generation and solar had also done well, and that while Eskom had managed to avoid load shedding during the day, reinstating Stage 4 only for the peak and evening, the loss of two units on Friday morning would require Stage 1 load shedding during the day on Saturday and Sunday with Stage 4 kicking in at 16:00 on both days ; said planned maintenance had been around 2 500MW, typical of Eskom's winter plan, and that the lower-than-anticipated demand was also partly due to the implementation of the Eskom 18.6% tariff increase, which took effect on 1 June.

a7038.speaker: Survey undertaken by Eskom and the industry associations for wind and solar PV power
a7038.name: Survey undertaken by Eskom and the industry associations for wind and solar PV power
a7038.speech: Found that 66 000MW of renewable energy projects were in development across the country.

a7067.speaker: GSM Association (GSMA) 2024 report on the mobile gender gap
a7067.name: GSM Association (GSMA) 2024 report on the mobile gender gap
a7067.speech: Shows a large disparity: women in sub-Saharan African countries are 13 percent less likely to own a phone compared with men, while the difference in mobile internet use is 32 percent ; although phone ownership among women has increased, in sub-Saharan Africa 71 percent of women own a mobile phone compared with 82 percent of men, and approximately 200 million women in sub-Saharan Africa are still not connected to internet services, while for all developing countries the figure is 785 million.

a7067.speaker: GSM Association (GSMA) 2024 report on the mobile gender gap
a7067.name: GSM Association (GSMA) 2024 report on the mobile gender gap
a7067.speech: Explains that this gap has a major impact, increasing economic inequality and preventing women's participation in the fast-growing digital economy.

a7067.speaker: GSM Association (GSMA) 2024 report on the mobile gender gap
a7067.name: GSM Association (GSMA) 2024 report on the mobile gender gap
a7067.speech: Reports that the digital gap is caused by several barriers including cost, digital skills, social norms and safety: among women interviewed in Senegal, 56 percent cited skills as a major barrier compared with 40 percent of men; in Pakistan, 19 percent of women cited the culture of their community as a major barrier to using mobile internet compared with four percent of men; and many women have greater safety fears about using the internet than men, including concern about online harassment, breaches of privacy and online fraud.

a7067.speaker: GSM Association (GSMA) 2024 report on the mobile gender gap
a7067.name: GSM Association (GSMA) 2024 report on the mobile gender gap
a7067.speech: Estimates that 32 low- and middle-income countries could lose more than 500 billion dollars in Gross Domestic Product (GDP) within the next five years because of the digital gender gap ; added that women, who are a large part of the agricultural workforce, often miss the opportunities mobile technology offers farmers because of a lack of access to phones, something that reduces their productivity and income.

a7067.speaker: Professor Aurelia Kamuzora, expert in economics and business
a7067.name: Professor Aurelia Kamuzora
a7067.title: expert in economics and business
a7067.speech: Says this problem is both global and national, since women have been left behind, especially in the ownership of property, because of existing cultures which have kept women behind; she says this happens even within the family: if one item is obtained, the father will be the first to own it rather than the woman, because they believe he is the one who can use it well. "Even if it is the woman who was given that gift, if her husband does not have one she will give it to her man first in order to ensure that there is equality." ; Says the issue of income within the family is also a challenge, making the little that is obtained fall into the man's ownership - even when a house is built it will be registered in the man's name, something that can also happen with a phone, which may be bought in the man's name but used by the woman.

a7067.speaker: Professor Aurelia Kamuzora, expert in economics and business
a7067.name: Professor Aurelia Kamuzora
a7067.title: expert in economics and business
a7067.speech: "If we can reduce this we will have helped women and given them great capability, because communication is business, education and empowerment; whoever communicates must be needed in society because he or she has capability, so if a woman is helped with communication she will be able to help the family, raise the family well, and grow the economy by doing business."

a7067.speaker: Vodacom Tanzania
a7067.name: Vodacom Tanzania
a7067.speech: Acknowledges that the findings of the research reflect the situation in Tanzania; explains that it believes in connecting people to digital services in order to grow the economy and intends to leave no one behind, and that in collaboration with the Tanzania Women Chamber of Commerce it has provided communication solutions including internet services, mobile phones, bulk SMS and M-Pesa available throughout Tanzania; it aims to end the challenge of low phone ownership among women by providing affordable phones.

a7067.speaker: Vodacom Tanzania sustainability (ESG) report, signed by Managing Director Philip Besiimire
a7067.name: Vodacom Tanzania sustainability (ESG) report
a7067.title: signed by Managing Director Philip Besiimire
